THE ERASURE AUDIT TRAIL IS DESTRUCTIBLE -- refutes the v4 design of record. dev/design/0.8.20-erasure-and-h-end-state-v4.md section 3.6 asserts excise_source_audit 'retains source_id PERMANENTLY (:6479) -- by design; that is the audit trail', and plan-0.8.20.md section 8 repeats it as the justification for the non-PII source_id rule. VERIFIED FALSE at 4ca70ba6: the audit row is written into operational_mutations (engine lib.rs:6479), and enforce_provenance_retention (:10070) sweeps THAT SAME TABLE cap-first, oldest-id-first, with NO COLLECTION FILTER (:10083-10089: DELETE FROM operational_mutations WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM operational_mutations ORDER BY id LIMIT ?1)). Erasure audit rows are swept like any other op-store row. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (1) ACCOUNTABILITY GAP -- demonstrating THAT an erasure occurred is a distinct obligation from performing it; a retention sweep can silently destroy the proof. (2) COLLISION WITH WORK ITEM 9 -- excise_collection_record operates on the op-store, the SAME table the audit rows live in, so the erasure record and the payloads being erased share one retention pool. The non-PII source_id rule STILL STANDS (an unswept audit row may still hold it) but its stated rationale is argued from a false premise and must be corrected. RECOMMENDED (HITL, decision owed): exempt the erasure-audit collection from enforce_provenance_retention by filtering the sweep by collection, and state the audit-durability guarantee explicitly. This is a RETENTION-POLICY change, not a pure defect repair, hence HITL-gated.

PROCESS: committing a codex transcript into the reviewed range pollutes the NEXT review's diff. TC-RUBRIC-7 requires persisting every codex section-9 transcript to a durable release-namespaced path. At 0.8.20 Slice-0 the transcript was committed to dev/plans/runs/codex/0.8.20/ and the fix-1 RE-review was then run with the same '--base 4ca70ba6'. Because the base was unchanged, the re-review's diff INCLUDED the previously-committed transcript file, so codex re-read its own prior findings as though they were part of the change under review -- the old [P2] finding text reappeared verbatim in the new transcript, which is easy to misread as 'the finding was not fixed'. It was fixed (verified independently: pre-fix exit 128, post-fix exit 0 under codex's own reproduction), and codex's actual terminal verdict was PASS. MITIGATIONS (pick one, for every later slice): (a) re-review against a base that already contains the prior transcript, (b) persist transcripts on a path excluded from the review scope, or (c) commit transcripts only AFTER the slice's final review round. Recommend (c) as the simplest: it keeps the reviewed diff to real code+docs and still satisfies TC-RUBRIC-7 at slice close. Also note the transcript path was pinned as .log (not .md) to match the existing 0.8.16-slice-*-codex-review-*.log convention and stay out of markdownlint scope.

ROOT CAUSE: the eu7 harness CANNOT COMPLETE ON CPU on this box -- BATCH=256 exceeds its own hardcoded 600s drain timeout at the measured embed rate. Measured at 4ca70ba6 by bisecting N (three runs): n=7667 FAILED, n=200 FAILED, n=20 PASSED. All three failures are identical: panic at eu7_real_corpus_ac.rs:414 'seed drain (batch): Scheduler' == engine.drain(600_000) -> wait_for_idle timed out -> EngineError::Scheduler. THE WORKER IS NOT WEDGED: n=20 passed cleanly (exit 0, vector_stage recall@10 = 1.0000, 258.54s) so the embed/projection path is FUNCTIONALLY CORRECT. It is THROUGHPUT. The n=20 run reports seed_ms=111670 for 20 docs = 0.179 docs/sec, which is ~7.3x SLOWER than the 1.3 docs/sec the harness docstring assumes (:97-99). At 0.179 docs/s a BATCH of 256 needs ~1430s, so it can NEVER drain inside the hardcoded 600_000 ms -- the harness is STRUCTURALLY unable to run here regardless of N, because failure happens on the FIRST batch. Full 7667-doc seed would need ~11.9 HOURS even if the timeout were raised. NOT a weights problem (cache complete: config.json + tokenizer.json + model.safetensors present) and not CPU contention (load 4.5 of 24 cores). OPTIONS for Slice 40: (a) reduce BATCH 256 -> 64 (64/0.179 = 358s, fits inside 600s) or make BATCH/timeout env-tunable -- minimal, surgical, does NOT change measurement semantics; (b) raise the drain timeout and accept a ~12h CPU run; (c) investigate the 7x throughput shortfall vs the documented rate, which may itself be a real CPU-embed regression worth catching. RECOMMEND (a)+(c). NOTE THE TENSION: TC-12 forbids running eu7 on GPU for comparability, and CPU cannot finish -- so R-20-EU7 has NO runnable path until this is fixed. Slice 40 must not treat this as optional. SIDE-EFFECT HAZARD: the harness WRITES dev/plans/runs/eu7-latest-measurements.json into the repo on every run, so a reduced-N scouting run silently produces a file that LOOKS authoritative (the n=20 run wrote recall=1.0000 there). Consequence: a consumer can QUERY by validity window but cannot SET one — validity is not end-to-end usable from Python/TS/Rust. Tests author windows via direct SQL on a closed DB. summary: napi #[napi(object)] Option::None OMITS the property — it is not null; ToNapiValue governs bare returns only
body: MEASURED, after two wrong theory-driven type claims in one slice. napi-derive-backend 1.0.75 codegen/struct.rs obj_field_setters emits 'if field_.is_some() { obj.set(..) }' for use_nullable==false — None SKIPS the set, so the JS property is ABSENT (not null, not present-and-undefined). The else-branch emitting Null only exists under use_nullable=true, which appears ZERO times in fathomdb-napi. napi 2.16.17 ToNapiValue for Option<T> DOES map None->null, but #[napi(object)] fields never reach that impl (it governs bare returns / nested positions) — conflating the two is the trap. Convention in this repo: the public TS layer MANUFACTURES null via '?? null' (index.ts ceScore); a bare passthrough leaks undefined. Any future #[napi(object)] Option field must normalize with '?? null' or declare the field optional. STALE PROSE NOT FIXED: Rust doc comments on SearchHit.ce_score (fathomdb-napi/src/lib.rs:540-541) and PerHitExplain still say 'null' where native truth is 'absent'.

summary: R-20-PR registry shape: plan's roles:{filterable,rankable,searchable} as three booleans CANNOT express the ratified C-1 contract — must be a SET of typed roles
body: ORCHESTRATOR DESIGN FINDING, code-grounded, for whoever builds R-20-PR/R-20-EAV. plan-0.8.20.md §1/§3 summarises the registry as 'ProjectionSpec {name, roles: {filterable, rankable, searchable}}'. Read as three booleans that is UNBUILDABLE against the RATIFIED C-1 contract, for three independent reasons. (1) C-1 Q4's whole tiering mechanism is 'declare the cheap roles now, ADD the vector role at promote(), drop on reject' — that REQUIRES searchable->FTS and searchable->vector to be SEPARATELY declarable; one 'searchable' boolean cannot express it. (2) The staleness contract (projection-registry-and-async-embed.md §3) splits them by guarantee: filterable + searchable->FTS are SAME-TRANSACTION, searchable->vector is ASYNC carrying dense_readiness. (3) Slice 20 (R-20-DR, dense_readiness + atomic flip) attaches ONLY to searchable->vector — a boolean gives Slice 20 nothing to attach to. C-1 Q1 also fixes the wire shape: Memex ALREADY LANDED 'AttributeSpec.index: Set[ProjectionRole]' inert at memex 95ed450, so the engine must accept a SET or the ratified cross-repo seam does not connect. Recommended: enum ProjectionRole { Filterable, SearchableFts{tokenizer:Option<String>}, SearchableVector{embedder:Option<String>}, Rankable } with roles as a set; absent tokenizer/embedder => engine default (C-1 'Tokenizer/embedder defaults' section). summary: R-20-PR: 'filterable' has TWO incompatible backends — vec0 pre-KNN filtering cannot be extended without a full re-embed; ADR-0.8.11 D3 forbids the post-KNN fallback
body: ORCHESTRATOR DESIGN FINDING, code-grounded. The 'filterable' role resolves to storage through TWO different, incompatible engines today. (A) SEARCH/vector backend: vector_filter_clause (engine lib.rs:8685-8710) is a HARDCODED four-column map onto vec0 metadata columns {source_type, kind, created_at, status}. vec0 is a virtual table with NO ALTER, so adding a fifth filterable field on the pre-KNN path means DROP+RECREATE vector_default and RE-EMBED THE WHOLE CORPUS — per registration. Unacceptable. (B) read.list backend: Predicate::to_sql_clause emits json_extract(body, path) gated by the COMPILE-TIME const PREDICATE_PATH_ALLOWLIST (lib.rs:1808) of exactly six paths. The obvious escape — join EAV after the KNN — is EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN by ADR-0.8.11 D3 no-demotion, which is enforced in the type system: a Json filter term is TYPE-REJECTED on the vector backend (lib.rs:2038-2044). So all three options are constrained and the tension is REAL, not incidental. NOTE the C-1 contract describes filterable as a 'pre-KNN constraint' (projection-registry-and-async-embed.md §2), i.e. backend (A) — the expensive one. ORCHESTRATOR RECOMMENDATION (NOT ratified, owed to the HITL): scope filterable to backend (B) for 0.8.20 — the registry supersedes the compile-time PREDICATE_PATH_ALLOWLIST with a runtime-registered set, and the vec0 metadata filter set stays FROZEN at its four columns. This is a DEVIATION from the contract's pre-KNN wording and must be ratified, not assumed, because Slice 30's H7 can-i-deploy gate checks as-built against that contract.

summary: TC-33 migration story worked out: node/edge temporal split CONFIRMS the INTEGER recommendation; blast radius is small in schema but crosses an external BYO-LLM wire format
body: ORCHESTRATOR DESIGN WORK on the HITL-directed harmonisation. CONCLUSION: converge on INTEGER epoch seconds, i.e. the Steward recommendation STANDS — no escalation of the direction call is required on the merits. SCHEMA BLAST RADIUS IS SMALLER THAN FEARED: exactly ONE table, TWO columns (canonical_edges.t_valid/t_invalid, TEXT, added by step 14), and ZERO indexes reference either column, so no index rebuild is forced. BUT the real cost is NOT the schema, it is FIVE surfaces: (1) 8 SQL predicate sites that today inline datetime('now') (engine lib.rs:7806, 9553, 9685, 10074, 10112, 10903, 10970, 4539) must switch to a BOUND :now — which is a strict improvement, it is what makes edge validity deterministically testable the way node validity already is; (2) PreparedWrite::Edge t_valid/t_invalid Option<String> -> Option<i64>, a breaking binding-coordination change; (3) ConsolidateCandidateEdge AND its harness JSON contract (lib.rs:4405-4406) which is an EXTERNAL BYO-LLM wire format; (4) temporal_fallback is derived by STRING EQUALITY comparing t_valid against warnings[].substituted_t_valid (lib.rs:4302-4305, 4123-4141) and BREAKS SILENTLY under a type change — this is the sharpest edge and needs its own RED test; (5) two tests that deliberately PIN the TEXT representation (s22_edge_temporal_columns_are_untouched_text in schema/tests/step22_migration.rs:211, r_20_nv_edge_temporal_filter_is_unchanged in engine/tests/slice10_node_validity.rs:624) must be rewritten, not deleted — they were the drift guard and must be replaced by an INTEGER equivalent. LAYERING CALL OWED TO THE HITL: storage and the governed SDK surface should both become INTEGER, but the BYO-LLM EXTRACTOR JSON should KEEP ISO-8601 with engine-side normalisation on ingest — an LLM cannot reliably emit epoch seconds, and that boundary already has a normalisation layer. This is a layering boundary, not splitting the difference on the representation; flagging it explicitly because it is adjacent enough to the direction call that the HITL should confirm it. MIGRATION MECHANICS: SQLite has no ALTER COLUMN TYPE, and the pinning test asserts declared type == TEXT, so true harmonisation requires a 12-step TABLE REBUILD of canonical_edges (create-new / copy-with-conversion / drop / rename), not an UPDATE in place. HAZARD: strftime('%s', x) returns NULL on an unparseable value, and a NULL t_invalid READS AS 'still valid' — so a junk value silently RESURRECTS an invalidated edge. That must be a RED test and a migration-time hard failure, never a silent NULL. SCHEDULING NOTE: this needs schema step 24 (23 being the EAV/registry step), making FOUR migrations in 0.8.20. I-6 'one migration per release' is GUIDANCE, not enforced — there is no test counting steps per release, and 0.8.20 already ships two (21 and 22), which dev/plans/0.8.6-0.8.16-PROGRAM-SEQUENCING.md:417 explicitly blesses. So four is precedented but should be surfaced, not slipped through.

summary: strftime('%s',?) used as an ISO-8601 validator but SQLite's date parser is MORE LENIENT than the declared contract — codex found 3 leniencies across 2 rounds; safety-critical no-NULL property intact (wrong-instant, not resurrection)
body: TC-33 normalises edge timestamps by delegating to SQLite strftime/date fns, leakier than strict ISO-8601: (1) too-large epochs [fixed fix-1]; (2) pre-year-0000 epochs render non-NULL '-001-12-31T23:59:59Z' so reject_unrenderable_edge_epoch (engine:1892-1894) passes them despite outside declared 0000..=9999; (3) bare numeric strings '0'/'2451545.0' treated as JULIAN-DAY -> epoch not NULL (engine:1824-1827), so non-ISO wire input stored as unrelated instant. SAFETY: none yield NULL t_invalid, so HITL Note1/P3 'no resurrection via NULL' INTACT — wrong-instant not fail-open. Root fix: strict ISO-8601 shape gate (regex, no dep) before SQLite, plus numeric MIN/MAX range check on governed i64 path. HALTED at fix-N bound (5th codex round) pending HITL/steward: consolidated root-cause fix vs accept-as-pre-1.0. Distinct from TC-43.

summary: Slice 15e gated vec0 filterable reshape: the ProjectionDestructive drop-list acknowledgement channel is defined for REMOVING a filterable but UNDEFINED for ADDING a net-new filterable that (per decision-4) still wipes all embeddings — needs a total ack channel; Steward direction owed
body: 15e must reshape vec0 to carry a registry-declared filterable attribute as a PRE-KNN metadata column (decision 2, ADR D3). Decision 4: the reshape does NOT preserve embedding blobs, so ANY filterable-set change (ADD or REMOVE) is destructive to the vector index and must be gated. Slice 15d's gate is ProjectionDestructive + an explicit drop-list — which names a projection to REMOVE. When ADDING a net-new filterable attribute there is nothing to put in the drop-list, yet the ADD still triggers a full embedding wipe, so it must be acknowledged. The drop-list channel is therefore undefined for the ADD case. Implementer recommendation (sound): a typed reshape-acknowledgement parameter on configure_projections (e.g. allow_reshape / a ReshapeAck), the only channel total across ADD and REMOVE — a GOVERNED-SURFACE addition needing sign-off. Also verified: vec0 rejects quoted column identifiers (attr cols need byte-safe encoding e.g. attr_<hex-of-utf8>); vec0 rejects partial-column INSERT (all ~6 INSERT sites must bind every attr col — inherently multi-site); the async projection worker carries no node body (write-path population is net-new); run_pin_and_requantize_pass (engine:8973) is a SAME-SHAPE re-quantize that must PRESERVE attr cols — decision-4 no-preservation applies ONLY to the filterable-set-change reshape, NOT to same-shape re-quantize (conflating would wipe attr values on every mean-pin). Proposed decomposition 15e-1 (shape param + gated reshape + pre-KNN compile, attr cols ship '' sentinel, population deferred — mirrors how Slice 10 shipped status) / 15e-2 (write-path + rebuild_vec0 population) / 15e-3 (governed filter-predicate + reshape-ack across Py/TS). 15e-1 is BLOCKED on this ack-channel decision.

summary: RESOLVED — HITL chose Option 1: NON-DESTRUCTIVE vec0 reshape. Ack-channel gap DISSOLVES (no new governed surface). NO-DATA-MIGRATION is scoped to the cross-version schema step, NOT a runtime reshape of a live DB. Follow migrate_vector_partition_pack1_to_pack2 (engine:13492).
body: The premise 'a reshape must wipe embeddings' was over-applying NO-DATA-MIGRATION (which governs the 0.8.9->0.8.20 cross-version schema step) to a RUNTIME reconfiguration. A non-destructive re-insert keeps old+new rows aligned/coherent/queryable, and the tree already ships exactly that op (pack1->pack2). So a filterable ADD reshape is NON-destructive => no acknowledgement parameter needed, no ProjectionDestructive for the ADD case; idempotent re-registration is a no-op; a shape change re-inserts non-destructively. FOUR load-bearing conditions (all must hold or results go SILENTLY wrong): (1) list rowid EXPLICITLY in the re-insert (rowid==write_cursor, engine:7086/:10005; auto-assign decouples embedding from node); (2) new attr column is plain metadata OR partition key, NEVER a vec0 aux/'+' column (aux hard-errors filtered KNN, engine:13460-13464 — this is what makes pre-KNN D3 work); (3) back-fill old rows with '' sentinel (vec0 TEXT metadata NOT-NULL-able, engine:7091) so they fail-to-match cleanly; (4) copy embedding_bin VERBATIM via vec_bit(...), do NOT re-quantize (re-deriving bits from raw embedding leaves old rows un-centered vs new mean-centered => incomparable Hamming, silent recall corruption; anti-pattern at engine:13584-13599). run_pin_and_requantize_pass is a separate same-shape op — leave alone. Scope: filterable already works via 15d EAV (canonical_attributes); 15e adds ONLY pre-KNN vector-path routing (D3, no post-KNN json_extract demotion).

summary: SURVIVING TEMPORAL P2 (calendar-rollover sub-class of TC-44): strftime silently ROLLS OVER a shape-valid impossible DAY (2025-02-30 -> 2025-03-02) instead of NULL; the is_iso8601_shape gate (fix-5) checks format, not calendar validity. ESCALATED per the ratified sixth-round rule (no reflexive temporal fix).
body: Verified vs SQLite: strftime('%s','2025-02-30T00:00:00Z') -> epoch that round-trips to 2025-03-02; '2025-04-31'->'2025-05-01'; but '2025-13-01' (month 13) -> NULL. So SQLite rejects impossible MONTHS but silently rolls over impossible DAYS. TC-44's fix-5 shape gate accepts 2025-02-30 (well-formatted YYYY-MM-DD), so a BYO-LLM edge timestamp of Feb 30 stores a DIFFERENT instant than the provider supplied — bypassing the hard-reject contract. SAFETY: the stored value is a valid instant, not NULL, so the 'no resurrection via NULL' property (HITL Note 1 / P3) HOLDS — this is wrong-instant, not fail-open. Clean complete fix available: a CALENDAR ROUND-TRIP (strftime the epoch back to a date and compare the date component to the input; reject on mismatch) closes the whole rollover sub-class, not another partial patch. Options for HITL/steward: (a) calendar round-trip validation [recommended]; (b) accept as documented pre-1.0 (safety intact); (c) rethink strftime-as-validator (no chrono/time in workspace by design). Per the ratified rule, this is a design call, not a reflexive fix. Distinct, non-temporal same-round finding: TS configure_projections wrapper skips validateFfiString (lone UTF-16 surrogate -> U+FFFD persists) — bounded AC-068 gate fix, folded into the closeout.

CAVEAT for every future path that enqueues projection work: drain never calls notify_new_work, so an enqueue that does not itself notify leaves the dispatcher asleep on pending_scan false and drain burns its ENTIRE timeout into EngineError::Scheduler. Confirmed live during Slice 20c - an early cut enrolled the vector kind AFTER collect_projection_jobs had already decided whether to wake the dispatcher, and the row sat enqueued in the database with the dispatcher asleep for the full 120s. The api-surface.md C4 rider deliberately forbids making drain a trigger - drain is a barrier, wait-for-idle - so the fix ALWAYS belongs on the enqueue side. Slice 20c fixed the paths it owns (configure_projections notifies after commit; late enrolment runs before collect_projection_jobs). ANY OTHER enqueue path that does not notify retains this defect. Rule of thumb for future slices: enqueue and notify are one operation, never two.

drain spins to its full timeout while ProjectionRuntime state.frozen is true. The dispatcher will not schedule while frozen, so a drain issued during a purge, erase, or rebuild window cannot make progress and returns EngineError::Scheduler rather than flushing. Freeze sites are in fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs around the purge and erase paths and in run_rebuild. Found during Slice 20c and deliberately NOT fixed there - drain passivity is protected by the api-surface.md C4 rider and the internal callers already drain BEFORE freezing. Worth deciding whether drain should return a distinct typed error while frozen instead of an indistinguishable timeout, since a caller cannot currently tell a frozen engine from genuinely slow embedding.

run_rebuild can return with re-enqueued embed work still outstanding. It drains BEFORE rebuild_shadow_state rewinds the projection cursor, and never drains after, so the rebuild replays work onto the runtime and then returns while that work is still in flight. It relies on set_frozen(false) setting pending_scan to get the dispatcher moving. Found during Slice 20c and not fixed there (out of slice scope). Consequence for callers: an operator rebuild is not a synchronous flush - a caller that needs vectors materialised must issue its own drain AFTER run_rebuild returns. Related to TC-61 (enqueue and notify coupling).

ProjectionRuntime::wait_for_idle has a lost-wakeup window that causes spurious slow drains and is a spurious-timeout risk for callers passing a short timeout. It releases the state lock to run database_has_pending_projection_work; a worker that finishes the last job inside that window notifies BEFORE the waiter re-acquires the lock, so the waiter misses the notification and sleeps the full remaining timeout before returning Ok. Measured during Slice 20c fix-1: the flush-barrier suite reported roughly 30s wall time with all assertions passing in about 40 percent of parallel runs (30.19s / 0.25s / 0.26s / 30.15s for the same test). Mechanism was confirmed by capping the cvar wait at 25ms - 6 of 6 runs then fast - and that one-line change was REVERTED because drain passivity is protected by the api-surface.md C4 rider and was out of the fix scope. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by 20c; 20c only widened exposure by adding engines to the suite. A caller passing a short drain timeout can get a spurious Err(Scheduler) purely from this race. Fixing it means re-checking the predicate under the lock or bounding the cvar wait.

CAVEAT for the slice that lands PER-ATTRIBUTE embedding: ProjectionSpec has NO kind axis, so Slice 20c had to guess the enrolment scope and the guess is load-bearing. The spec is name plus roles plus optional fts and vector sub-objects - per-ATTRIBUTE, with no kind - while derive_dense_readiness is documented as CORPUS-WIDE because 15d defers per-attribute embedding. Slice 20c therefore read a searchable-to-vector declaration as the corpus dense arm is live and enrolled every vector-eligible node kind present in canonical_nodes (its decision D1). That breadth directly produced BOTH codex round-2 findings: a P1 permanent wedge when a corpus contains a kind outside the resolve_source_type locked list, and a P2 false-ready on the late-enrolment path. Both were fixed in 20c fix-2, but the underlying seam remains: enrolment scope is inferred, not declared. When per-attribute embedding lands, the enrolment scoping and the readiness scoping must move together through the SAME seam, and this inference should be replaced by an explicit kind axis rather than re-derived.

TC-11 logical_id pin: the STATIC migration guard is a lexical scanner, not a SQL parser — known-open evasion shapes remain; the DYNAMIC whole-ladder test (D2) is the load-bearing, shape-independent proof
body: Landed at 0.8.20 Slice 25 (R-20-SUR). check_migration_logical_id_pin in src/rust/crates/fathomdb-schema/src/lib.rs statically rejects any migration step that would populate logical_id on an existing canonical row. It is a LEXICAL scanner (comment-strip, string-literal elision, quoted-identifier unwrap, schema-qualifier normalisation, statement split on ";") and therefore cannot be complete against SQL grammar. codex §9 produced FOUR same-family [P2] evasions across three fix rounds — schema-qualified names, UPDATE OR <conflict-action>, leading-CTE, and subquery-in-an-earlier-SET-expression. The first three are CLOSED; the fourth and the shapes below are KNOWN-OPEN and recorded in the function doc comment under "# Known limits": subquery in an earlier SET expression truncating the SET clause, a rename round-trip, and a CREATE TABLE AS SELECT swap. The run halted at the orchestration circuit-breaker (3 fix rounds on one finding) — a 4th round buys a 5th [P2]; Steward ruled ACCEPT the residual. WHY THAT IS SAFE: the requirement is NOT proven by the static guard. It is proven by the dynamic guard in fathomdb-schema/tests/slice25_logical_id_pin.rs — migrating_to_head_never_populates_logical_id_on_an_existing_node/_edge snapshot identity ROWS before and after migrating a real mixed anonymous/governed corpus through the whole ladder to head, and assert via fn null_to_not_null that NULL -> NOT NULL transitions == 0 plus byte-identical IdSpace::to_prefixed(). That compares rows, not SQL text, so it catches EVERY evasion the lexical guard misses, whatever its shape. D1 is defence-in-depth and a fast authoring-time fail; D2 is the proof. DURABLE CAVEAT FOR A FUTURE SLICE/RELEASE: do not treat a green static guard as evidence the pin holds, and do not delete or weaken the D2 whole-ladder tests to speed up the schema suite — they are the only shape-independent enforcement. If anyone wants the static guard to be actually complete, the durable fix is to parse the migration SQL with a real SQLite grammar rather than extend the lexical scanner; that is a net-new dependency and was explicitly out of scope for 0.8.20.

summary: MEASURED: reopening a database that has ANY enrolled vector kind costs 90 SYNCHRONOUS embeds inside Engine::open - the 0.8.18 vector-equivalence probe. This was previously unreachable in practice because nothing enrolled a node kind in production; Slice 20c gave _fathomdb_vector_kinds its FIRST production enrolment path (configure_projections declaring searchable-to-vector), so from 0.8.20 onward a normal consumer workspace can hit it on every open. Found while investigating the no-embedder enqueue question in 20c fix-3 and NOT fixed there (out of slice scope). Consequence: open latency becomes proportional to the equivalence-probe batch rather than constant, on a path consumers hit at startup. Worth deciding whether the probe should be sampled, made async, cached against a fingerprint, or skipped when the embedder identity is unchanged since the last open.

The EDGE projection path has the same unconditional-enqueue shape as the node path that Slice 20c fixed, and the un-stranding helper does not reach it. project_canonical_edge_row enqueues unconditionally, while reenqueue_stranded_vector_rows joins canonical_nodes ONLY - so gating edges alone would merely trade one permanent terminal for another rather than making edge embed work recoverable. PRE-EXISTING since G11; NOT introduced by 20c and deliberately not fixed there (20c scoped itself to the node path its own enrolment change created). A future slice that wants edge bodies to be recoverable after a no-embedder or failed session must extend the stranded-row query to canonical_edges at the same time as it gates the edge enqueue - the two must land together or the fix is a no-op.

PRE-EXISTING SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT race between a projection worker committing its terminal and a caller open write, already documented in slice20_dense_readiness.rs. MEASURED during 20c fix-4 while probing whether the embed retry ladder could be shortened for edges: shortening ONLY the edge ladder moved the worker terminal-commit into the window of a caller write and took consolidate_provider from 0 of 48 failures to 8 of 48 under 6-way concurrency (origin-main baseline is 0 of 48). The retry ladder was therefore LEFT AS SHIPPED and the race was not fixed - 20c deliberately did not touch it. CAVEAT for any future slice that wants to shorten, remove, or make adaptive the projection retry ladder (DEFAULT_PROJECTION_RETRY_DELAYS_MS): the ladder is currently acting as an accidental backoff that masks this race, so changing it WILL surface SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT failures under concurrency. Fix the race first, then the ladder - not the other way round.

OPEN codex section-9 [P2] from Slice 20c round 5, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED - the orchestration circuit-breaker was reached at 5 fix rounds. vector_projection_declared keys off the stored vector sub-object ALONE (vector_declared = 1) rather than requiring the searchable role, so declaring {roles: [filterable], vector: true} in a session WITH a live embedder will enrol vector kinds, backfill, and make later writes enqueue embeddings - even though that combination is documented as inert-but-round-trippable (the shipped Slice-15d contract pinned by vector_subobject_is_stored_not_built). The shipped inert test does not catch it because it runs without a live embedder. FIX: make the predicate require the searchable role, i.e. use the same active searchable-to-vector predicate everywhere. NOTE the blast radius - vector_projection_declared gates all three of the forward backfill path, the drop inverse, and late enrolment, so the change must be re-verified across all of them together. IMPACT is wasted embed work and unexpected vectors at rest for a projection meant to be inert; it is NOT a false-ready and NOT data loss, which is why it was judged lower severity than the four findings closed in rounds 1-4. Transcript: dev/plans/runs/codex/0.8.20/slice-20c-fix-5-rereview-20260726T224040Z.log

MEASURED: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast is NOT reliably green on this machine, on main as well as on a slice branch, so a single green workspace run is WEAK evidence. Controlled comparison run during the Slice 20c landing gate, same script, sequential, same load: the merged 20c tree failed 1 of 3 runs and plain main failed 1 of 3 runs. Each failure was a DIFFERENT concurrency-sensitive test - slice15e undeclared_after_concurrent_drop_is_typed_invalidfilter_not_storage_race on the merged side, t_s34_dump_mutations_lock_held_exits_71 on main, and lifecycle_observability in an earlier ad-hoc run - and EVERY one of them passes reliably in isolation (slice15e 6 of 6, lifecycle_observability 3 of 3). Conclusion: this is parallel-execution contention in the full-workspace run, NOT a regression from any one slice, and it is the same family as TC-70. CONSEQUENCE for future slices: do not treat a single red full-workspace run as a blocker without re-running the failing suite in isolation and comparing against a main control, and do not treat a single green run as proof. If the workspace gate is to be load-bearing for release DoD it needs the underlying races fixed or the run serialised.

summary: R-20-H7 gate maintenance contract: what it does NOT cover, the permanently-red assertion hazard, and the fixture coupling it introduced
body: Three durable properties of the can-i-deploy gate landed at Slice 30 that a later agent must not rediscover the hard way. (1) THE PERMANENTLY-RED ASSERTION HAZARD IS A CLASS, not a one-off. A can-i-deploy assertion keyed to a release action that has NOT HAPPENED YET holds the release forever. It bit this contract once already: pre-efa8d584 clause Q6(b) mandated anonymous surrogate minting that the ratified TC-11 pin forbids ever implementing. Slice 30 avoided three MORE instances of the same class: (a) the contract Landing section says C-1 co-lands at 0.8.20, but the manifests still read 0.8.9 until the Slice-40 bump, so the gate asserts C-1 CODE PRESENT ON THE 0.8.20 LINE and deliberately NOT a manifest version equality; (b) the per-projection vector embedder override is RECORDED BUT INERT (one engine-wide pipeline serves all vector projections), so the gate asserts only absent-implies-engine-default; (c) fts tokenizer override likewise recorded but deliberately not honoured, pinned to the 0.9.x multi-field FTS work. DO NOT TIGHTEN ANY OF THESE THREE into the stronger nearby statement. (2) THE GATE IS STATIC-STRUCTURAL AND SAYS SO. It asserts symbols, tables, negative-space greps, and for behavioural clauses that the NAMED TEST still exists - it does NOT re-execute those suites. Consequence worth naming: TC-71 (vector_projection_declared ignores the searchable role) breaks NO verbatim C-1 clause, so when Slice 21 fixes it this gate will neither notice nor object. Do not read a green H7 as evidence about TC-71 either way. (3) FIXTURE COUPLING INTRODUCED DELIBERATELY. Wiring the gate into preflight --landing turned four sibling suites red (test_preflight_landing, test_check_ledgers, test_check_board_currency, test_check_governed_surface_pin) because their throwaway fixture repos carry no C-1 subject and the gate correctly exited 2 under anti-fail-open. Repaired with a seeder scripts/tests/lib/c1-conformance-fixture.sh that COPIES the real artifacts, unlike its synthetic sibling lib/governed-surface-fixture.sh. That departure is forced, not lazy: the implemented-assertion set is a constant inside the gate and the registry bijection is rigid in both directions, so any pin not registering exactly the 26 CHECKABLE ids reports MALFORMED. If the clause registry ever changes, those four suites inherit the change through the seeder - expect it and do not weaken the gate to decouple them.

summary: Slice 30 hit the 6-round fix cap on a NON-engine slice with every round finding a new distinct defect — the TC-75 argument, outside TC-75 scope
body: ESCALATION CONTENT for the Steward, recorded durably so it survives the orchestrator returning. Slice 30 (R-20-H7 can-i-deploy gate) ran SIX codex section-9 rounds and halted at the per-slice total cap in orchestration.md section 6. The 3-same-finding bound NEVER fired. Each round found a NEW and DISTINCT false-negative class in the gate: round 1 regex shape plus open vocabulary; round 2 refinements of both (schema qualifiers, spellings outside a match arm); round 3 FILE SCOPE (negative probes read one lib.rs, missing a literal violation in a sibling module); round 4 SUBJECT BINDING (a probe bound to a file rather than to the thing the clause names); round 5 WRONG SUBJECT plus INACTIVE PROOF (fn_defined accepted a function with #[test] removed or #[ignore] added); round 6 a receiver-less fn_sig false green plus a nested-inner-attribute false RED. THE YIELD WAS REAL AND LARGE, which is why this matters: fix-4 alone found that EIGHTEEN OF TWENTY-SIX clauses had a demonstrable false green, every one closed with its own RED-first divergent fixture. The gate as first written would have been substantially decorative. Two weak probe kinds were deleted OUTRIGHT rather than left unused (file-scoped absent in fix-3, the count-based min in fix-4) and a third (fn_defined) was made unreachable for test paths. Fixture assertions grew 106 to 276. THE POINT FOR THE STEWARD: this is precisely the argument that produced TC-75 for engine slices - the total was cutting off a PRODUCTIVE loop rather than an unproductive one - but Slice 30 touches ZERO engine source, so the engine amendment does not reach it and the non-engine bound of 6 applied. The question to put to the HITL is whether the TC-75 reasoning should be re-expressed as a rule keyed to WHETHER ROUNDS ARE PRODUCTIVE (each finding new and distinct) rather than to WHICH DIRECTORY the slice touches. A gate/tooling slice that audits a whole contract surface has the same round-productivity profile as an engine slice. VERBATIM ROUND-6 FINDING (2), whose commit-message copy at e8e35260 was truncated by shell backtick substitution and is therefore recorded here in full: a pinned test file that later gains a nested module of the form - mod helpers open-brace hash-bang bracket cfg(feature = x) bracket ... close-brace - would be reported by fix-5 new file-level cfg check as wholly conditionally compiled, blocking CI and preflight even though the top-level pinned proofs still run. No such module exists today so nothing is red now; the fix is to scan only depth-0 header attributes. NEITHER round-6 finding makes the gate red on the current tree.

summary: ORCHESTRATION TRAP, self-disclosed by the Slice-30 orchestrator and reusable across every future run: an until-loop waiter written as until ! pgrep -f "codex exec review" CANNOT EVER SATISFY ITS EXIT CONDITION, because pgrep -f matches against full command lines and the waiter subshell CONTAINS that pattern in its own command line - so it matches itself and spins forever. Consequence in this run was wasted wall-clock only; the orchestrator disclosed that every green it reported was taken from direct git and gate polling rather than from those loops, and the Steward independently re-ran all eight gates in the worktree and reproduced exit 0 on each, so NO conclusion depended on the broken waiter. The reason to record it is that the pattern would SILENTLY HANG any future orchestrator that copies it, and a hung orchestrator is exactly the 36-hour silent-stall failure class this program already carries a memory about. FIX SHAPE: a pgrep guard must exclude self - match the binary rather than the command line, e.g. pgrep -x codex or ps -C codex, or add a negative pattern. Per the standing rule that guardrail failures are fixed in TOOLING rather than by telling agents to be careful, the durable fix is a documented wait-for-codex helper in the orchestration playbook rather than a warning; every orchestrator hand-rolls this loop today. Adjacent to TC-53, the ledgerwrite shell-substitution hazard, in that both are caller-side shell defects that a tool or helper could eliminate outright.

summary: TC-82 RULED (HITL 2026-07-28): AMEND - the fix-N cap keys on ROUND PRODUCTIVITY, not on which directory a slice touches
body: RULING: amend. The TC-75 engine amendment is re-expressed as a rule keyed to whether rounds are PRODUCTIVE - each round finding a new and distinct defect - rather than to whether a slice touches src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src. Basis, measured not argued: Slice 30 touches ZERO engine source and nonetheless ran seven rounds in which every single round found a new and distinct false-negative class in the gate, the 3-same-finding anti-thrash bound never fired once, and fix-4 alone showed eighteen of twenty-six clauses had a demonstrable false green. Directory is a poor proxy for risk; a gate or tooling slice auditing a whole contract surface has the same round-productivity profile as an engine slice. WHAT MOVES AND WHAT DOES NOT: the same-finding bound stays at 3 and is unchanged - it is the anti-thrash rule and three attempts at one defect means the design is wrong, not the patch. The per-slice default total stays 6. What changes is the predicate that permits extension to 10: formerly the slice path, now round productivity, with the mandatory Steward check-in at 6 becoming UNIVERSAL rather than engine-only. Beyond 10 remains an HITL halt. This codifies what actually happened on Slice 30, where the Steward check-in at 6 occurred at seq-124 and authorised a bounded seventh round.

summary: TC-84 RULED (HITL 2026-07-28): a mid-flight SendMessage steer does NOT count against the fix-N round cap; the residual is ACCEPTED-KNOWN
body: The step-7 question carried by the 2026-07-27-A hand-off as open decision 3, minted its own id here so the durable rule homes can cite it. RULING: a mid-flight SendMessage steer to an in-progress fix-N round does NOT count as a round and does not advance the cap counter. RECORDED IN THE OPEN - this is the OPPOSITE of the Steward recommendation, which was that drip-feeding inside one round should count. The Steward accepts the ruling and does not re-litigate it. ACCEPTED-KNOWN RESIDUAL, recorded so no future reader mistakes it for an oversight: because the counter advances only on rounds, an orchestrator can serially steer inside a single round and never trip the breaker. The cap therefore bounds ROUNDS, not correction volume. Anyone reasoning about the breaker should read it as a bound on review-verdict cycles, not on how much correction flows in one cycle. CONSEQUENCE: Option B Phase 2 agent-seat hardening is UNBLOCKED - it was blocked on exactly this semantics question.

summary: CODEX TRANSCRIPTS CAN CARRY FOREIGN SESSION DATA INTO A PUBLIC REPO - caught before landing, no prior exposure, needs a tooling guard
body: MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The ASH Phase-2 round-1 codex transcript arrived carrying 216 lines of raw Claude Code session JSONL. codex, running under --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, had run rg across ~/.claude and slurped the results into its own stdout, which the Steward then tee-d to a file destined for dev/plans/runs/codex/ - a tracked path. Those lines held conversation content from THREE PROJECTS OTHER THAN THIS ONE: agent-aware, local-unifi-openwrt, memex. github.com/coreyt/fathomdb is PUBLIC (gh repo view --json visibility -> PUBLIC), so committing them would have published another projects sessions, including a home-network project. CAUGHT BEFORE LANDING and redacted, with an in-file banner naming the count, the projects and the reason; the review verdict and all reasoning were preserved. NO PRIOR EXPOSURE, measured rather than assumed: git grep -l for lines beginning /home/coreyt/.claude/projects/ over dev/plans/runs/codex/** returned ZERO already-committed files. This was a first occurrence. WHY IT WILL RECUR WITHOUT A GUARD: the mechanism is structural, not a one-off mistake. Every codex section 9 review in this repo is invoked with --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, which is what lets it read outside the repo at all; TC-RUBRIC-7 then requires the terminal transcript to be persisted under a TRACKED path; and nothing between those two steps inspects what the transcript contains. Any reviewer prompt that makes codex search broadly for context can reproduce this, and the person committing is looking at a verdict at the end of a multi-megabyte file. Per the standing principle that a guardrail failure is fixed in the tooling and not with a be-careful note, the disposition should be a mechanical check rather than guidance. PROPOSED, NOT DECIDED - the Steward is bringing this to the HITL: a pre-commit or agent-lint check that HARD-fails when any file under dev/plans/runs/codex/ contains lines matching the home-slash-.claude-slash-projects shape, or more generally any absolute path into a users Claude Code state directory. Cheap, mechanical, and it fails closed. Natural home is DOC-HYGIENE-3, which is already sequenced after Slice 31 and already carries the TC-53 ledgerwrite id fix. body: Landed on main. What began as a near-miss uncovered a real, already-public exposure. Seven committed transcripts carried directory inventories slurped by bypass-sandboxed codex reviewers; one was ls of the users whole projects directory, which had published 33 PRIVATE PROJECT NAMES including a client-named one to a PUBLIC repo for roughly three weeks. All removed via the tools own --redact, preserving each transcript as evidence per TC-RUBRIC-7 and stating counts and reasons without re-typing the names. STEWARD-VERIFIED ACROSS ALL TRACKED FILES, not the edited blocks: ten representative names each git grep to ZERO; ordinary words bosun wake memex local were checked individually and legitimate prose left untouched; verdicts and review reasoning survive in every redacted file. THE GATE HAS TWO PREDICATES sharing one lib so filter and gate cannot drift - agent-state paths, where FOREIGN hard-fails including the tool-results shape and OWN-PROJECT warns with the self-exemption PRINTED ON EVERY RUN rather than hidden in a regex; and out-of-repo directory inventories, hard-fail with no own/foreign split. Dual-homed into agent-test.sh, preflight --landing and an always-on CI job. Capture-time layer folded into the already-mandated codex-nostdin.sh wrapper with the exit code preserved via PIPESTATUS. A SUBAGENT REPORTING ERROR IS RECORDED: fix-3 claimed the foreign names were all at zero; that did NOT reproduce - it had verified against the block it edited rather than the whole file, and the Steward caught it, which is what surfaced the far larger ls-projects exposure underneath. HONEST LIMITS: redaction does NOT unpublish, the names were public for three weeks and history forks and caches retain them, so this stops propagation only and a history rewrite was considered and NOT taken; the gate cannot see a bare directory listing with no output block, only --redact aimed by a human; preflight does not relay WARN lines on a clean tree. CODEX SECTION 9 WAS NOT RUN on this branch - disclosed, not omitted - under an explicit HITL directive to finish, the acceptance criterion being mechanical and Steward-verified directly. Gates all 0: transcript-hygiene, its 223-assertion suite, preflight --landing, seat-path-guard, c1 fixtures, lint-md.

summary: Do NOT triage a codex review by grepping [P1]/[P2] markers over the transcript - the tally is dominated by the CODEBASE'S OWN provenance comments, which use the identical format. Measured: fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs alone carries 21 [P1] and 101 [P2] markers.
body: MEASURED, on the Slice 21 round-1 review (dev/plans/runs/codex/0.8.20/slice-21-review-20260728T184947Z.log, 228,792 bytes, CODEX_RC=0). The Steward tallied markers over the transcript as an independent cross-check on the orchestrator's triage and reported a floor of 3 [P1] / 25 [P2]. That interpretation was WRONG and the orchestrator corrected it. The true distinct finding set was 0 [P1] / 1 [P2]. TWO compounding causes, and the second is the durable one: (1) codex double-emitted its own finding block verbatim, so even its real output over-counts; (2) THE DOMINANT CAUSE - codex cat/rg'd lib.rs into the transcript, and this repo deliberately annotates fixes with their review provenance in the SAME syntax ('// 0.8.20 Slice 21 fix-1 (codex section 9 round 1 [P2], ledger TC-71)', '// fix-5 (codex section 9 round 4 [P2])'). Verified independently by the Steward against the branch: git show orch-0.8.20-s21:src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs | grep -oE '\[P[12]\]' yields 21 [P1] and 101 [P2] IN THE SOURCE FILE ITSELF, before any review runs. Regions codex reads twice are counted twice. CONSEQUENCE: a marker tally over a transcript measures how much source codex echoed, NOT how many findings it raised, and it fails in the DANGEROUS direction - it inflates, so it manufactures phantom P1s and can push a slice toward a fix round it does not need or make a clean review look alarming. It also cannot be fixed by de-duplicating near-identical lines, because the noise is legitimately distinct source lines. WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: read codex's own verdict/'Review comment:' blocks, which are structurally distinguishable from echoed source, and reconcile any count against the orchestrator's triage rather than asserting it over the top. DO NOT 'fix' this by stripping provenance markers from source comments - they are load-bearing (they tell the next agent which review round produced a line, which is exactly how the TC-57 stale-517 comment trap was caught). The tallying method is what is broken, not the annotation convention. Applies to any future agent building an automated review-triage or a marker-count gate.

summary: ledgerwrite updates a .seq SIDECAR that nothing makes you commit - stage the .jsonl alone and you strand it, which breaks preflight --landing on main for the NEXT agent, not yourself. Happened twice in one session. Place the fix in DOC-HYGIENE-3 beside TC-53.
body: MEASURED, twice in the same session, by the same actor (the Steward), which is the point - discipline did not prevent the second occurrence twenty minutes after the first. MECHANISM: dev/agent-tools/ledgerwrite/ledgerwrite.py appends to <ledger>.jsonl AND writes the max seq to a sibling <ledger>.jsonl.seq sidecar. The natural git incantation after a ledger append is 'git add dev/steward/steward-ledger.jsonl' - the sidecar is a separate path, is not implied by it, and nothing warns. Both commits 41a81c17 (steward seq-131) and 3e660f95 (todos TC-87) staged the .jsonl and left the .seq behind. BLAST RADIUS, and why this is worse than a private mistake: the ledger-integrity check in scripts/preflight.sh --landing HARD-fails when a sidecar disagrees with max(seq), so a stranded sidecar breaks the LANDING GATE ON MAIN FOR EVERY SUBSEQUENT AGENT while the actor who caused it sees nothing wrong. It surfaced here only because the Slice 21 orchestrator hit exit 1 at its push and correctly refused to clear a ledger it had been told was not its own - a well-behaved halt is the ONLY reason this was caught rather than compounding. Verified at the time: working tree sidecars 131/122, committed 130/121, actual max(seq) 131/122. REMEDY OPTIONS, cheapest first, none implemented: (a) a pre-commit hook that refuses any commit staging a ledger .jsonl without its .seq sidecar - mechanical, catches it at the moment of the mistake, mirrors how the repo fixed other guardrail failures; (b) ledgerwrite itself runs 'git add' on both files after a successful append, so the pair can never separate; (c) drop the sidecar and have preflight derive max(seq) from the .jsonl directly, removing the duplicated state that can drift at all - the cleanest, but changes the integrity check's contract and needs a look at what else reads the sidecar. PLACEMENT: DOC-HYGIENE-3, beside TC-53 and the ledgerwrite duplicate-id hole - same file, same class of missing guard, one visit. DO NOT fix this by telling agents to remember the sidecar; that is the failure mode this repo has already ruled against (guardrail failures are fixed in tooling, not with a be-careful note).

summary: TC-57 CLOSED and LANDED in Slice 21 (77be504b). The race is fixed by BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the governed arm of commit_batch - AND the characterization CORRECTED this entry's own mechanism claim: it is plain SQLITE_BUSY (5), NOT SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT (517), at 10/10 not 7-of-8.
body: The ruled characterize-first ordering (steward seq-111, HITL 2026-07-26) paid for itself here and this is the durable lesson. THE CORRECTION: every prior write-up - this TC-57 entry, the anon_node comment in slice20_dense_readiness.rs, and the OOS-17 note in lib.rs - named SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT (517) as the mechanism. Measured, that is only ONE of two un-retryable exits from a lock promotion and it is NOT the one the engine takes. The engine returns plain SQLITE_BUSY (extended code 5) IMMEDIATELY, with the busy handler invoked ZERO times. A fix scoped to 'retry on 517' would have shipped INERT - passing review, closing the ticket, fixing nothing. Both code comments were corrected in-slice; this entry is the ledger half. MEASURED at 41a81c17: repro arm (logical_id Some) 10/10 failures, control arm (logical_id None) 0/10, failure message byte-identical across all ten runs - deterministic at this shape, not intermittent, and always the third write of a governed ingest loop. Prior claim was '7 of 8'. ROOT CAUSE: the governed branch of commit_batch READS BEFORE IT WRITES inside a BEGIN DEFERRED transaction, so it must promote a read lock to a write lock while the async projection worker is active; busy_timeout cannot save a promotion. FIX: R1 - BEGIN IMMEDIATE for the governed arm, taking the write lock up front. Verified to the characterization's own acceptance bar (doc section 1.4), not one lucky run: repro 0/10, control 0/10, three tc57_mechanism_* pins green, OOS-17 regression guard rc 0. That bar matters because of TC-72 - cargo test --workspace is not a stable signal in this repo, so a single green proves nothing on a concurrency fix. FULL CHARACTERIZATION: dev/design/0.8.20-tc57-write-race-characterization.md (519 lines, proven/not-proven labelled, five remedies enumerated with NONE implemented before the ruling). FOUR ITEMS CARRIED FORWARD, unfixed, recorded in STATUS-0.8.20.md section 18 and NOT part of this close: the ~50 percent baseline duplicate-embed rate (present in the anonymous arm too, so unrelated to TC-57), silently-discarded worker commit failures, Engine::transition's still-DEFERRED read-then-upgrade transaction, and R2 bounded retry pending an error-path restructure. Placement of those is a Steward call, pending.

summary: TC-71 CLOSED and LANDED in Slice 21 (77be504b). vector_projection_declared now requires the searchable role - and codex round 1 caught that gating the DECISION without reconciling ALREADY-ENROLLED state left the entire harm intact on upgrade.
body: Left OPEN at the Slice 20c five-round circuit breaker, closed here. THE BASE FIX: the predicate keyed off the stored vector sub-object alone, so {roles:[filterable], vector:true} activated the dense arm instead of staying inert. It now answers through the typed registry (roles is persisted as a comma-joined sorted string and is NOT a trustworthy SQL predicate - a LIKE would match a forward-compat token that merely CONTAINS a role spelling). Re-verified across all three paths the predicate gates: forward backfill, drop inverse, late enrolment. The RED test runs with a LIVE embedder, because the shipped inertness test passes VACUOUSLY without one. THE FINDING THAT MATTERED (codex section 9 round 1, the single distinct finding of the review): the base fix corrected the DECISION to enrol but not the ALREADY-ENROLLED STATE. lib.rs:17550 gates the enqueue solely on _fathomdb_vector_kinds membership, and vector_kind_needs_enrolment tests kind_is_vector_indexed BEFORE reaching the new predicate, so an already-enrolled kind never sees the fix; the only un-enrol path fires on a before-and-not-after transition. Net: a database that had already run the old code KEPT EMBEDDING under inert declarations - TC-71's entire stated harm surviving its own fix, for exactly the users who already had it. Fixed at open time (RED f70f00bf, GREEN 3349344b), not overridden. TWO IMPLEMENTER CORRECTIONS TO THE ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN BRIEF, both load-bearing: (1) the legacy-database safety argument was WRONG - schema step 24 CREATES the registry table on every open, so a legacy DB boots with the table present but EMPTY and the table-exists probe never protects it; EXISTS(vector_declared = 1) is the sole protection, audited against the four at-risk suites; (2) reconciliation in apply_projection_config had to be 'before OR predicate', not a replacement - the predicate alone would have REGRESSED the shipped drop case, since dropping the last projection carrying a vector sub-object leaves the EXISTS condition false. Neither implies the other. ALSO: absolute embed counts are unusable as an oracle across a reopen, because run_vector_equivalence_probe re-embeds 45 references on any open with a non-empty _fathomdb_vector_kinds; every embed assertion is now a DELTA from a post-open snapshot.

summary: TC-83 WIDENED: the self-matching-process trap is NOT pgrep-specific. pkill -f <pattern> matches its OWN command line too and kills the calling shell - observed live (exit 144) in the Slice 21 orchestrator, which had been briefed against the pgrep form and still hit the pkill form.
body: ORIGINAL TC-83: 'until ! pgrep -f "codex exec review"' can never exit, because pgrep -f matches the command line of the shell running the loop, so the wait hangs forever and silently stalls any orchestrator that copies it. WIDENING, measured during Slice 21: the same defect in pkill is WORSE than a hang. The Slice 21 orchestrator ran pkill -f "waiter_exited" to clean up its own bounded waiter; the pattern matched the pkill invocation's own command line and it killed its own shell (exit 144). It had been explicitly briefed against TC-83 in the pgrep form by the Steward and still hit it, because the entry named pgrep and the agent reached for pkill - so the write-up, not the agent, is what failed. THE GENERAL RULE, which is what should be carried forward: any -f / full-command-line process matcher (pgrep -f, pkill -f, ps | grep, killall against a pattern) matches the matching process ITSELF. Match the BINARY instead (pgrep -x codex, ps -C codex), or exclude self by pid. The Steward's own waiter in the same session used pgrep -x codex and was unaffected, which is the working pattern to copy. RELATED, same session, same class: 'rc=$?' placed after a pipe reports the LAST element's status, not the command's - the orchestrator read tail's exit as a merge's and a conflicted merge briefly registered as rc 0. Capture rc on the very next line, before any pipe or command substitution.

summary: plan-0.8.20.md section 9's 'IMMEDIATE NEXT' pointer is HAND-WRITTEN while release-state-<release>.json already owns next_slice - it went stale at two consecutive landings in one session, and commission-manifest.sh cites that section as a brief's MANDATE anchor, so the staleness is COPIED INTO THE NEXT COMMISSION. Make it a generated view. DOC-HYGIENE-3.
body: MEASURED TWICE IN ONE SESSION. (1) At the Slice 21 commission the section still said 'IMMEDIATE NEXT: Slice 30' although Slice 30 had landed at 9b3ed0e3; caught and fixed at 62486a01 BEFORE briefing, but only because the Steward happened to read the anchor the manifest cited. (2) Immediately after the Slice 21 landing it said 'IMMEDIATE NEXT: Slice 21' - stale again, within hours. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ORDINARY DOC ROT: scripts/commission-manifest.sh resolves '## 9. Immediate next slice' as the {{MANDATE}} anchor for an orchestrator brief. The manifest's own CHECK 2 verifies that the anchor EXISTS, not that its CONTENT is current - a heading cannot rot, but the prose under it can, and does. So the generated, path-verified brief hands an orchestrator a hand-written pointer at the wrong slice, with the manifest's authority behind it. DOC-HYGIENE-2 already solved exactly this class for four other regions: release-state-<release>.json is the single writer and scripts/check-release-state-views.sh renders marker-delimited blocks from it, HARD-failing on any drift or hand-edit. next_slice is ALREADY a field in that file and is ALREADY kept true at every landing. This pointer is simply not yet one of the rendered views. REMEDY: add a generated_views entry rendering the 'IMMEDIATE NEXT' line (and ideally the remaining-ladder line beside it) from next_slice + remaining_ladder + the ladder titles, then the drift becomes mechanically impossible rather than a thing each Steward must remember at land time. INTERIM MITIGATION, already applied: a visible warning blockquote sits above the pointer telling the reader to re-verify against next_slice before commissioning, and the STATUS board's next-action cell now carries the same instruction. Those are notes, not controls - the generated view is the control. Same class as TC-88: a fact duplicated in two places with nothing checking they agree.

summary: Engine::transition still runs a read-then-upgrade transaction under BEGIN DEFERRED - the SAME defect class TC-57 just fixed in commit_batch, in a second location, UNFIXED. Found by the Slice 21 orchestrator, carried forward in board section 18, no owning plan.
body: TC-57's root cause was that the governed branch of commit_batch READ BEFORE IT WROTE inside a BEGIN DEFERRED transaction, forcing a read-to-write lock promotion while the async projection worker held the write lock - which SQLite refuses with plain SQLITE_BUSY (5), immediately, with the busy handler never invoked. Slice 21 fixed that ONE call site with BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Engine::transition has the SAME shape and was NOT touched. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN SLICE 21: correctly out of scope - the slice's ruled legs were TC-57, ac_002 and TC-71, and widening an engine slice mid-flight is exactly the scope creep the repo forbids. It is recorded here rather than left in the board's close record because board section 18 is a CLOSE RECORD for a landed slice; an agent scoping 0.8.21 or a later concurrency slice will read the todos ledger, not the section 18 of a slice that closed months earlier. STATUS: not characterized - no repro exists for the transition path, and TC-57's own lesson is that the mechanism must be MEASURED before a fix is scoped (the prior write-ups named SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT/517 and were wrong, which would have made an obvious fix inert). Do NOT assume the commit_batch remedy transfers unexamined. PLACEMENT IS AN OPEN STEWARD/HITL CALL: it is a real defect on the concurrency path of a publishing release, but 0.8.20's remaining ladder is 22 -> 31 -> DOC-HYGIENE-3 -> 40 and none of those own it; the natural candidates are a 0.8.21 concurrency slice or a scoped addition, and adding scope to a ruled slice is an HITL decision, not a Steward one.

summary: Two further vector/worker defects carried forward from Slice 21, both unfixed and unowned: (a) the ~50 percent BASELINE duplicate-embed rate, present in the ANONYMOUS arm too so NOT TC-57's doing, and (b) projection-worker commit failures silently discarded via 'let _ = commit_projection_outcomes(..)'.
body: Both surfaced during the Slice 21 investigation, both correctly left out of scope, both recorded in board section 18 - which is a close record, not a work queue, so they are lifted here. (a) DUPLICATE EMBEDS: roughly half of embeds at BASELINE are duplicates. Critically this reproduces in the ANONYMOUS arm as well, so it is NOT caused by the governed-write race TC-57 fixed and did not go away with it. Impact is wasted embed work - the same harm class as TC-71, at a different layer - and it is invisible to correctness tests because a duplicate embed produces the right answer, just twice. Note the interaction with TC-68 (Slice 22): run_vector_equivalence_probe already re-embeds 45 references on ANY open with a non-empty _fathomdb_vector_kinds, which is a separate known source of repeat embedding that TC-68 is scheduled to cache away; whoever takes this must separate the two before attributing a rate. (b) SILENTLY DISCARDED WORKER COMMIT FAILURES: the projection worker's commit path is invoked as 'let _ = commit_projection_outcomes(..)', so a failure to commit projection outcomes is dropped on the floor with no error, no log and no telemetry. Consequence: the worker can fail to persist its work and nothing anywhere reports it - and, as the Slice 21 orchestrator found the hard way, it also means measuring worker risk via 'failed' terminal states is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of seeing this class, because the failure never reaches a terminal state at all. That second point is the durable one: any future attempt to quantify worker reliability by counting failed terminals will report a falsely clean number until this is fixed. (c) ALSO CARRIED, lower priority: TC-57 remedy R2 (bounded retry on the busy codes) remains unimplemented pending an error-path restructure; R1/BEGIN IMMEDIATE shipped instead and closed the measured defect, so R2 is an option not an obligation - see the five-remedy enumeration in dev/design/0.8.20-tc57-write-race-characterization.md section 7.

summary: Requirement ids are never BACK-LINKED into the design docs they depend on, so commission-manifest.sh HARD-FAILED on Slice 22 (zero design docs matched TC-67/TC-68/R-20-VC) even though the design of record exists for every leg. Fixed for 22 by annotating 5 docs; the discipline gap is unfixed.
body: MEASURED at the Slice 22 commission. scripts/commission-manifest.sh 0.8.20 22 exited 1: 'ZERO design docs matched 0.8.20 Slice 22 (tokens: TC-67, TC-68, R-20-VC)' - its TC-37 vacuous-pass guard, working exactly as designed, refusing to emit a brief whose required-reading list would be empty. THE GUARD WAS RIGHT AND THE ALARM WAS REAL, but the underlying diagnosis is NOT 'the design does not exist'. It exists for all four legs and was found in minutes: TC-67 -> record-lifecycle-protocol/projection-registry-and-async-embed.md (registry/declaration semantics) plus 0.7.0-vector-quant-pack1.md (the home of resolve_source_type and of the D3 partition-key lock the leg must NOT touch); TC-68 -> 0.8.18-slice-5-vector-equivalence-probe.md (the probe itself); decision #18 -> errors.md (canonical error-type ownership); sqlite-vec #99 -> vector.md (vec0 storage). NONE of them mentioned TC-67, TC-68 or R-20-VC, because the manifest selects design docs by LITERAL TOKEN MATCH on TC/requirement ids and those ids were minted 2026-07-27, long after the docs were written. So the scan cannot see a dependency that runs BACKWARD IN TIME - which is the normal direction for a reserved-gap slice consuming older design. CONSEQUENCE, and it is bimodal: a slice with zero matches HARD-FAILS and cannot be commissioned at all (loud, recoverable - this case); a slice with ONE weak incidental match emits a brief whose required reading is thin but LOOKS complete (quiet, and worse). Slice 21 was the second shape: it matched exactly one doc, orchestration.md, on the token TC-71, and the manifest itself printed 'NO design doc mentions: ac_002, TC-57, R-20-CR'. That line was correct and was easy to read past. FIXED FOR SLICE 22, bookkeeping only: a 'Requirement traceability' blockquote added to each of the five docs naming the requirement/TC it serves, explicitly marked as added by the Steward with no design change. Verified: manifest now exits 0 with 5 docs, 3 classified / 2 unclassified, statuses reported honestly (locked / draft / UNREVIEWED with the TC-50 pointer) - nothing laundered as design-of-record that is not classified. THE DISCIPLINE GAP IS UNFIXED: nothing requires a back-link when a requirement id is minted. REMEDY OPTIONS: (a) at requirement-mint time (the plan's reserved-gap section), require the minting agent to back-link each new id into the design docs the leg depends on - cheapest, and it is a checklist item at exactly the moment the knowledge exists; (b) let the state file carry an explicit design_refs list per slice, so the manifest reads a curated set instead of guessing by token match - removes the guessing entirely; (c) leave selection by token but make a slice with FEWER THAN N matches WARN loudly rather than pass quietly, closing the dangerous quiet mode. (b) plus (c) is the strongest pair. Natural home: DOC-HYGIENE-3 beside TC-89, which is the same failure shape - a fact the manifest depends on, maintained by hand, with nothing checking it.

body: RAISED BY THE HITL when ruling on the publish decision, in the words "it might be correct to do a Slice 4x and resolve the dependabot items". Recorded so the idea is not lost in a transcript. summary: commission-manifest.sh CANNOT CITE dev/adr/** or dev/interfaces/** AT ALL - DESIGN_ROOT is dev/design only, so ruling ADRs are unreachable by construction at any status, no matter what is back-linked. It also cannot see bare-number legs (#18, #99), and a full token match SUPPRESSES its own honest "NO design doc mentions" warning. DOC-HYGIENE-3 candidate.
body: FOUND by an independent HITL-directed audit of the Slice 22 design-of-record set (2026-07-28), and verified. THREE DISTINCT DEFECTS in the same selector, all worse than TC-92s back-link gap because no amount of back-linking fixes them. (1) UNREACHABLE TIERS: commission-manifest.sh sets DESIGN_ROOT=dev/design and scan_design walks only that tree, so dev/adr/** and dev/interfaces/** can never appear in a brief. For Slice 22 alone that permanently excludes the RULING ADR for decision #18 (ADR-0.6.0-error-taxonomy.md, status accepted, whose per-module-vs-direct-variant rule decides the family split), the HITL-SIGNED authority for TC-68 (ADR-0.8.18-vector-equivalence-self-check.md), the identity definition TC-68s fingerprint must key on (ADR-0.6.0-vector-identity-embedder-owned.md, accepted), and the canonical vec0 metadata-column table for #99 (ADR-0.8.11-filter-grammar-unification.md). It also excludes dev/interfaces/*.md, which carries the LITERAL #18 statement at rust.md:213-215 and :352 - and AGENTS.md:25 obliges those files to be updated when an error surface changes, an obligation TC-39 already records as routinely missed. An ADR is a HIGHER tier of authority than a design memo, so the manifest is blind to exactly the strongest evidence. (2) BARE-NUMBER LEGS ARE INVISIBLE: slice_tokens derives tokens by regex from the state-file title; the shapes #18 and #99 match none of its patterns, so two of Slice 22s four legs contributed NOTHING to selection and no doc could ever be matched for them. (3) THE HONEST WARNING IS SUPPRESSED BY SUCCESS: the manifest prints NO design doc mentions: <tokens> only for tokens with zero matches. Slice 21 got that line and it was correct and load-bearing. Once every derived token matches at least one doc, the line disappears - so a brief whose coverage is THIN but nonzero looks identical to one that is complete. This is precisely the dangerous quiet mode TC-92 named, and the Steward walked straight into it: the TC-92 back-link fix made all three Slice-22 tokens match and thereby SILENCED the warning. Self-inflicted, recorded so it is not repeated. REMEDY: TC-92 option (b) - an explicit design_refs list per slice in release-state-<release>.json - closes all three at once, because a curated list is tier-agnostic, needs no token shape, and makes coverage explicit rather than inferred. TC-92 options (a) and (c) close NONE of them. Recommend (b) as the primary remedy for both TC-92 and this entry, with a warn-below-N as a cheap secondary. PLACEMENT: recommend DOC-HYGIENE-3 alongside TC-53/88/89/92 (HITL ruled that scope at steward seq-137) - but that ruling named four ids, so adding a fifth is an HITL call and is NOT assumed here.

summary: TC-67 CLOSED in Slice 22 (572475f2). ProjectionDelta.vector_unsupported_kinds - sorted, deduped, empty-not-absent, OUTPUT-ONLY, additive and NON-ERRORING. Vocabulary NOT grown, Pack-1 D3 lock untouched, readiness semantics pinned in all three languages. The C-1 graceful-graft contract (Q4/Q6a) is preserved - verified byte-level by the Steward.
body: The Steward steered this leg mid-flight (not a fix round, TC-84) after an independent audit found the commission manifest had omitted a load-bearing constraint: the ratified OPP-12 C-1 contract Q4/Q6(a) requires a projection the engine cannot honor to be DEFERRED with NO ERROR and NO BUILD, and that clause is byte-pinned by scripts/c1-conformance-pin.json and mechanically asserted by check-c1-conformance.sh (ProjectionDelta.deferred: Vec<String> plus two named tests) as R-20-H7, a PUBLISH PRECONDITION. A report implemented as an ERROR, or by restructuring deferred, would have turned that gate RED. The reconciliation held: "report, not silent" and "no error, no build" are compatible, and the delivered report is additive and non-erroring. STEWARD-VERIFIED AT THE LANDING, mechanically rather than on the orchestrators word: the contract file, c1-conformance-pin.json and check-c1-conformance.sh are all BYTE-UNTOUCHED between 0cf2923c and b32e38ca, and check-c1-conformance.sh exits 0. summary: sqlite-vec vec0 DELETE defect: REPRODUCED AND LIVE - erase_source AND purge both returned Err(Storage) and LEFT THE ROW AT REST. A GDPR-ERASURE VERB, FAILING, IN THE RELEASE THAT PUBLISHES. Fixed engine-side in Slice 22 (572475f2) across all six by-rowid delete sites. Upstream is #274, NOT #99 - a mis-citation this repo carried for months.
body: COMMISSIONED AS A PROBE - "record a written finding either way". It came back red against two shipped erasure verbs, so the orchestrator kept the fix rather than shipping a finding; the Steward RATIFIES that deviation, because publishing knowingly-broken erasure to three public registries is not a defensible alternative. MECHANISM, pinned to upstream source: sqlite-vec 0.1.7 vec0Update_Delete_ClearMetadata (sqlite-vec.c:8888) deletes the _metadatatext<NN> shadow row for a TEXT metadata value longer than the 12-byte inline view, then returns sqlite3_step s SQLITE_DONE (101) VERBATIM - it never resets rc to SQLITE_OK. vec0Update_Delete (:9027) reads 101 as an error and aborts the whole DELETE. The INSERT/UPDATE twin is saved by an unconditional rc = sqlite3_blob_close(..) after its switch, so ONLY DELETE carries it. FATHOMDB EXPOSURE: the 0.8.20 Slice-15e attr_<hex> filterable columns - values are CALLER-SUPPLIED and stored marker-encoded (\\x01 || V), so any raw attribute value of 12+ bytes breaks every by-rowid DELETE FROM vector_default. MEASURED BOUNDARY on the real engine: raw 11 -> stored 12 -> Ok; raw 12 -> stored 13 -> Err(Storage), with the vec0 row AND its shadow value left at rest. That is data that survives an erasure request. FIXED across all six by-rowid delete sites with a tripwire test asserting the UPSTREAM defect still exists, so the workaround is removed deliberately rather than rotting. THE CITATION CORRECTION MATTERS FOR THE BUMP DECISION: the repo has tracked this as "sqlite-vec #99" throughout; the real upstream issue is #274. 0.1.8 STILL CARRIES IT; 0.1.9 FIXES IT. No dependency bump was taken in Slice 22 - that is an open HITL call, and the TC-76 re-open trigger has FIRED.

summary: EmbedderIdentity has NO normalization (or backend/device) field. TC-68 fingerprints cover that axis via the live mean_vec bytes IN PRACTICE, not BY CONSTRUCTION. A backend/device descriptor on EmbedderIdentity is the only thing that RETIRES the residual.
body: ADR-0.6.0-vector-identity-embedder-owned defines identity as (model_identity, model_version, dimension, normalization), but the shipped EmbedderIdentity struct has no normalization field - so a change on that axis is not structurally part of the identity. TC-68s cache compensates by including the live mean_vec bytes and the stored baseline blobs, which detects such a drift EMPIRICALLY. That is a sound mitigation and it is what shipped, but it is a probe, not a guarantee: it detects a change that has already altered the vectors rather than declaring the identity that produced them. Adding a backend/device descriptor to EmbedderIdentity closes it structurally. Relevant to the CPU/CUDA story: CPU and CUDA are 1-bit identical today, so a device descriptor would NOT currently change any fingerprint - it would make the invariant explicit rather than accidental.

summary: THREE test-harness traps measured in Slice 22, each of which makes a green or a red LIE: ac_029 is a WALL-CLOCK RATIO assertion that fails when a reviewer runs concurrently; src/python pythonpath=["."] SHADOWS an installed wheel and kills the X1 Python route with a misleading circular import; six engine targets exit 101 WITHOUT RUNNING absent --features operator.
body: All three measured during the Slice 22 build; recorded because each produces a signal that reads as the opposite of the truth. (1) ac_029 IS A WALL-CLOCK RATIO ASSERTION. REMEDY: word-boundary matching (re.search with \\b or an explicit token regex per pattern) rather than the `t in text` substring test. A stress arm (2 threads x 24 burst, 0 ms embed) returns 10/10, with its control at 0/10. So an agent instructed to "follow the TC-57 template", which is what the Steward wrote into the Slice 23 commission, would have concluded transition is CLEAN and filed a false negative on a real defect. THE TEMPLATE NEEDED A STRESS ARM AND THE COMMISSION DID NOT SAY SO. Recorded so the next characterization inherits the corrected protocol rather than the one that would have missed this. REPRODUCTION IS THE BAR, NOT RATE: the failure RATE does not replicate across sessions on the same commit and a quiet machine (5.9/40 vs 3.8/40), while REPRODUCTION held 10/10 in both. Any future acceptance criterion that gates on a rate will flake; gate on reproduction. Consistent with TC-72 (cargo test --workspace unstable ~1 run in 3) and TC-97 (ac_029 is a wall-clock ratio) - this repo cannot gate on timing-derived numbers. MECHANISM, measured: primary DatabaseBusy, extended code 5 - plain SQLITE_BUSY, NOT the SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT (517) that the pre-TC-57 write-ups all named - busy handler invoked 0 times, failing in 0 ms against a 5000 ms busy_timeout. Identical in kind to what TC-57 measured in commit_batch, which is why the classes are the same. A SECOND, DISTINCT DEFECT: transition never calls emit_sqlite_internal_error, so the SQLite extended code is NEVER PRODUCED - the race is not merely unfixed, it is undiagnosable from the outside, which makes the next investigation harder than TC-57s was. BEGIN IMMEDIATE TRANSFER MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, exactly as the commission required: transition -> Err(Storage) in 0 ms; the already-IMMEDIATE Engine::write -> Ok after waiting ~935 ms. The Slice 23 orchestrator recorded it as PRESUMED-NOT-MEASURED in the characterization document and refused to promote it, which is the correct handling and the reason it is trustworthy enough to record at all.
