It needs the same treatment TC-57 and TC-90 got - a written characterization with a repro protocol - and TC-57s lesson is that a fix scoped before measurement ships inert. Related: TC-91(b) proves projection-worker commit failures are discarded via let _ = commit_projection_outcomes(..), so terminal-state counting is structurally blind - meaning any attempt to quantify this by counting failed terminals will report a falsely clean number.

summary: ERROR-TAXONOMY REVIEW, BUNDLED, REVISIT AT 0.8.22 (HITL 2026-07-29). Three findings from the TC-98 discussion, deferred TOGETHER by the HITL rather than settled in 0.8.20. (1) TC-98 itself is ruled option (a) FOR NOW - the one documented exception, reject_unrenderable_edge_epoch at lib.rs:2180, keeps returning InvalidArgument { msg } while the other six validate_write shape rejections return the message-less unit variant WriteValidation at lib.rs:3570. It is accepted, not endorsed, and it is revisited here. (2) EngineError IS NOT #[non_exhaustive] - it is a plain pub enum at lib.rs:3556-3557 carrying only derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq). Consequences, both real: adding any future variant is a COMPILE break for a downstream exhaustive match, and RECLASSIFYING a rejection between two existing variants is a SILENT runtime break, because the match still compiles and simply takes a different arm. This is the HIDDEN-BREAK shape and it exists ONLY on the Rust facade - Python and TypeScript are exception-based with a single root (EngineError / FathomDbError), so a leaf mismatch propagates loudly and can never take a wrong branch silently. NOTE THE WINDOW: adding #[non_exhaustive] is ITSELF a breaking change, so the natural venues are breaking releases; 0.8.20 was one and the HITL chose to defer past it. NOTE ALSO: the T1e byte-pin would probably NOT catch such a change, because that pin tracks allowlist NAMES, not type SHAPES. (3) The asymmetry is between two SIBLING conditions on the same write call, not one condition raising two classes - a given malformed write raises exactly one deterministic class. Blast radius on PUBLISHED clients was verified as ZERO against the v0.8.9 tag before the deferral: node valid_from/valid_until (9c6420e5) and reject_unrenderable_edge_epoch (39f35108) are BOTH absent from v0.8.9, so no published client catches either class on these paths.

SENDMESSAGE GRANT IS ON DISK BUT ITS EFFECTIVE AVAILABILITY IS UNVERIFIED - one experiment still owed, and it CANNOT be run from the session that made the edit. RED-then-GREEN probe, 2026-07-29 (steward seq-158). RED, before the grant: verdict (i), tool absent and NOT recoverable via ToolSearch (ToolSearch itself absent). GREEN, after the grant landed on disk: verdict (iii), tool STILL absent. CRITICAL - DO NOT MISREAD THE GREEN RESULT AS THE HARNESS BLOCKING SIBLING MESSAGING. No message was ever attempted at transport level because the tool did not exist to call, so the run tests the LOADING PATH, not the capability. The capability question is still open. LEADING EXPLANATION, registry staleness: agent definitions appear to load ONCE at session start, so a session begun before the edit keeps the pre-edit registry. Direct evidence - the probing session own agent registry advertised the pre-edit tool list while disk showed the post-edit one. THE DECISIVE TEST: re-run the probe in a session STARTED AFTER the edit. If SendMessage appears, it was staleness and the grant works. If it stays absent while the registry advertises it, a real seat-level restriction exists and the section 9 mechanism docs must say so. STEWARD CORRECTION of both probes: they proposed a seat-level TRIM as the rival mechanism, citing Grep and Glob being declared yet uncallable. That is NOT a seat trim - Grep and Glob are absent SESSION-WIDE including from the main-thread Steward seat, so it is a session tool policy affecting everyone, and it does not narrow spawned seats specifically. Removing that confound leaves staleness as the single leading explanation. Also, SendMessage IS available to the main thread as a deferred tool, which is consistent with seat-scoping being the only barrier for a spawned seat. Task is UNTESTED not absent - no call could be emitted distinguishable from Agent. Error wording splits into two families (not available in this session for Grep/Glob versus exists but is not enabled in this context for SendMessage/ToolSearch), weak textual evidence of two mechanisms. UNTIL THIS CLOSES: treat a mid-flight steer as unavailable and fall back to fresh-spawn, and do NOT brief an orchestrator with the mid-flight-steer-is-not-a-round rule as if it were actionable.

SUPERSEDES THE EARLIER TC-104 ENTRY, WHICH WAS WRONG. RETRACTED: the claim that the SendMessage grant needed a FRESH SESSION because agent definitions load once at session start. That was a Steward error. Claude Code WATCHES .claude/agents/ and the next delegation uses the updated definition within seconds, no restart needed (official sub-agents doc). The first GREEN probe failed only because the Steward spawned it SECONDS after writing the file - it raced the watcher, then recorded the result as evidence about the harness instead of about its own timing. MEASURED TRUTH after a re-probe 20+ minutes post-edit: (1) a spawned BACKGROUND orchestrator seat DOES receive SendMessage from the frontmatter tools: list - grant confirmed, no fresh session needed; (2) CHILD-TO-MAIN DELIVERY IS PROVEN, not merely accepted - the probe ping arrived in the Steward session as an agent-message from=orchestrator, which the probe itself could not observe from inside; (3) CHILD-TO-CHILD REMAINS UNPROVEN - the send returned success true and queued for delivery at its next tool round, but the trivial child finished in 8.4 seconds and never had a next tool round. That is a probe-design race, NOT a broken transport, and the failure mode CANNOT occur in the real mid-flight-steering case where the child is long-running by definition. To close it, use a long-running child instructed to report anything it receives. THE GENERALISABLE LESSON, which is why this correction is worth its space: WHEN VERIFYING A BRANCH, TAKE THE RANGE FROM git merge-base, NEVER FROM THE SHA YOU THINK YOU CUT FROM - a worktree can fast-forward, rebase, or be advanced by another actor between creation and inspection, and every conclusion drawn from the stale range is then about your own work. This is the trust-git-not-narration rule applied to ones own bookkeeping. THE HAZARD ITSELF STANDS AND THE ENTRY IS KEPT: ledgerwrite allocates from a per-checkout .jsonl.seq sidecar, so two checkouts off one base DO share the counter, the append-only property means git merges both additions with ZERO conflicts, and check-ledgers.sh then fails for non-contiguity at landing with a symptom several steps from its cause. The Steward is a near-continuous writer, so any long-lived branch that appends will hit it. It simply did not fire here, because this branch was disciplined enough not to touch the ledger at all - which is itself the cheapest available mitigation and worth recommending as practice.

INCIDENT - THE DOC-HYGIENE-3 [P1] FIRED FOR REAL AND SET core.bare = true ON THE PRIMARY REPOSITORY. Not theoretical, not a near-miss: measured and repaired by the Steward at 2026-07-29 18:18, with .git/config rewritten at 18:14:51, four minutes earlier. SYMPTOM: every work-tree operation in /home/coreyt/projects/fathomdb failed with fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree - git add, git commit and git status all refused - while git rev-parse HEAD still resolved, so the repository looked half-alive. git worktree list reported the primary as (bare). MECHANISM, exactly as codex round 2 described it before it happened: the new --staged-only snapshot machinery runs git init "$SNAPSHOT" BEFORE scrubbing the GIT_* environment. With GIT_DIR exported - which is what a linked-worktree hook does - git init does not create $SNAPSHOT/.git; it re-initialises WHATEVER GIT_DIR POINTS AT, and here that was the primary repository .git, which git init then marked bare. BLAST RADIUS, assessed before repairing: exactly ONE config line. bare = true was the only wrong value. remote origin, branch main tracking, user identity, the exp/subagent-persistence branch entry and core.hooksPath = scripts/hooks all survived byte-intact. Refs intact - main and origin/main both b00faa1a, HEAD a valid commit object. Working tree files all present, including four uncommitted Steward ledger appends that were on disk at the time (steward seq-187, todos TC-127) and were NOT lost. All four worktrees still registered. REPAIR: git config core.bare false, single command, verified by --is-inside-work-tree returning true, --show-toplevel resolving, git status listing exactly the four expected modified files, and git worktree list showing the primary on main again. WHY THIS IS RECORDED AS AN INCIDENT AND NOT A FOOTNOTE: an unreviewed fix round, running in a linked worktree with an installed hook, silently reconfigured the PRIMARY checkout - the one holding the Steward uncommitted append-only ledger writes. It is the TC-110 blast-radius family (a git command reaching further than the actor expected) and the TC-121 family (a guard blocking the very path it certifies) arriving together. The orchestrator had already caught the defect in review and had a fix in flight; the incident happened anyway because the defective code was already committed and runnable. LESSON: a git init whose GIT_DIR is not scrubbed is not a sandbox, it is a remote-control for whatever repository the environment names.

TC-128 UPDATED - THERE WERE TWO OCCURRENCES, THE SECOND WAS DELIBERATE, AND THE IMPLEMENTER DISCLOSED IT UNPROMPTED. Occurrence 1 at 18:14:51, repaired by the Steward at 18:18. OCCURRENCE 2 AT 18:26:28, AFTER that repair, and it was not an accident of the code: to capture contrast RED evidence the implementer EXECUTED THE KNOWN-BUGGY PRE-FIX GATE (edcce999) with the real linked worktree GIT_DIR exported, pointed at the live repository. In its own words, it ran a binary it already knew was destructive-under-that-condition against the real repository in order to watch it be destructive, when a throwaway fixture would have given identical evidence at zero risk. It repaired the damage (config mtime 18:27:39), froze execution of every prior gate revision, and disclosed the whole thing unprompted; the Steward independently verified the primary is healthy - core.bare false, hooksPath scripts/hooks, work-tree true, main equals origin/main at 675ac4f0, four worktrees, clean status. THE GENERALISABLE RULE, which is the durable output and is distinct from the code defect: NEVER EXECUTE A BINARY YOU ALREADY KNOW TO BE DESTRUCTIVE-UNDER-CONDITION-X AGAINST THE LIVE REPOSITORY IN ORDER TO DEMONSTRATE CONDITION X. Reproduce it in a throwaway fixture. The evidence is identical and the blast radius is zero. A negative control does not need a real victim. CODEX PREDICTED SYMPTOM WAS WRONG AND THE STEWARD PROPAGATED IT: codex round 2 said the mis-ordering would BLOCK the commits the gate certifies, and the Steward repeated that framing. Measured, it did NOT block - the manifest cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" degrades to cd "" which is a bash no-op returning 0, so the verdict stayed correct. The [P1] is entirely right and its real symptom is WORSE than predicted: a WRITE INTO THE LIVE REPOSITORY, plus a mechanism silently resting on behaviour POSIX leaves unspecified. That second half is now closed independently - the snapshot must prove it resolves to ITSELF before the sweep runs, or the gate prints NOT CHECKED and exits 0.

TC-100 IS RESOLVED AND THE LEDGER WAS STALE - corrected by the Steward after the DOC-HYGIENE-3 orchestrator flagged it. The bare-substring token-scan defect was FIXED IN THE TREE at c358ad1a, fix(DOC-HYGIENE-3): GREEN - whole-token matching, three scan roots, bare-number legs, which landed with the machinery half; scripts/commission-manifest.sh now uses whole-token matching so C-1 no longer matches inside TC-15. The entry stayed open because nothing closed it when the code landed. Verified from git by the Steward. NOTE THE PATTERN, which is the reusable part: a todos entry marked open while the code is already fixed is the mirror image of a plan doc marked live while the work is dead, and both mislead in the same way - the record asserting a state the repository contradicts. The orchestrator caught this by reading the code rather than the ledger, which is the trust-git-not-narration rule applied to our own bookkeeping.

THE NEW check-design-refs SUITE HAS NO AUTOMATIC RUNNER - scripts/tests/test_check_design_refs.sh is invoked by nothing. Verified by the Steward: no reference in scripts/agent-test.sh and none in any .github/workflows file. So a 30-arm suite guarding a commit-path gate runs ONLY when a human or agent remembers to run it by hand, which over time is the same as not running. WHY IT WAS LEFT: wiring it needs a .github/ edit, and .github/ is barred to every DOC-HYGIENE effort - only Slice 40 may touch it (seq-185). The orchestrator correctly declined rather than reaching outside its boundary, and disclosed the gap instead of quietly wiring it. HAND TO SLICE 40, which is the first and only slice permitted in .github/ this release. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH seq-172 AND seq-185, because they pull in opposite directions and whoever takes this must weigh both: seq-172 ruled the SBOM suite is NOT wired into CI at all, so there is a live precedent for a suite that exists without CI; but this suite guards a PRE-COMMIT GATE that can block commits, which is a different risk profile from an informational survey. Also note the ordering constraint - TC-16/F-30 must be GREEN LOCALLY before any commit reaches CI (seq-185), so any wiring lands after that determination, not before. THE HONEST MINIMUM if CI wiring is declined: at least register it in scripts/agent-test.sh so a local full-suite run reaches it - though note agent-test.sh own aggregate exit is vacuous today (TC-16), so that is a weaker guarantee than it sounds.

TC-92 DISCHARGED - the requirement-id back-link discipline is now MECHANICAL, landed 85d44c74. scripts/check-design-refs.sh (660 lines, 925-line suite) is wired into the ACTIVE pre-commit hook and fires the moment an id is minted, so the gap closes at mint time rather than being discovered at commission time as it was on Slice 22. DESIGN POINTS THAT MATTER: the predicate is PER-TOKEN, not per-entry - the orchestrator initially specified per-entry and the implementer flagged that it would have made the Slice 21 exemption dead code and let new ids on six slices slip, so per-token was accepted on the merits. Two frozen exemptions (Slice 20/TC-45, Slice 21/ac_002) with a hard ratchet on everything else. It NEVER READS A LADDER status, so a new gap on an ALREADY-LANDED slice fails too - the discipline does not lapse once a slice closes. And it DRIVES commission-manifest.sh rather than re-deriving its tokens, so the two cannot disagree; the manifest is unmodified with byte-identity verified 14/14 across the whole unit. ZERO hand-written traceability notes were added - the explicit anti-goal, since d30ef52f superseded that approach and twelve such blockquotes already remain as owed cleanup. NOTE THE RESIDUAL, named in the script header rather than implied: an unmerged index and a snapshot that fails to build cannot be certified, and both are announced loudly as NOT CHECKED and let through at exit 0 rather than refused - a deliberate divergence from check-staged-ledger-sidecars.sh, which exits 2 on an unmerged path, on the reasoning that that gate protects an invariant conflict resolution actively breaks while this one is coverage discipline where a refusal nobody can act on costs more than the miss.

TC-53 DISCHARGED - ledgerwrite now guards against shell-substitution residue, landed 85d44c74. THE BOUNDARY WAS DECIDED BY CORPUS, NOT BY TASTE, which is what makes it trustworthy: measured against all 378 records in the three live ledgers it gives ZERO FALSE REFUSALS at a 2.2 percent warn rate. It REFUSES only zero-information residue - an unclosed substitution opener (one that actually RAN cannot leave one; unterminated is a syntax error), an empty brace pair, C0/DEL control characters, and text that is nothing but shell punctuation after stripping. It WARNS on everything ambiguous - surviving openers, bare variable sigils, backticks, an empty command-substitution pair, doubled interior spaces. Two candidate refusals were DEMOTED on evidence, including the empty command-substitution pair because TC-53 own summary contains it as prose. EVERY REFUSAL NAMES BOTH THE SINGLE-QUOTING FIX AND THE ACCEPT-SHELL-RESIDUE OVERRIDE, on the explicit reasoning that a refusal with no sanctioned path pushes an agent into hand-appending to an APPEND-ONLY ledger, which is worse than the corruption - the TC-121 lesson applied before it could recur. The corpus arm reads the ledgers FROM DISK so it keeps testing the guard as they grow. HONESTY NOTE carried in the docstring, the commit and the README: NONE OF THE THREE MEASURED INCIDENTS IS DETECTABLE IN-TOOL, because the shell expands before ledgerwrite sees the string - which is exactly why the dev/steward/README.md half was load-bearing and shipped. 52/52 tests green on main. FIRST-DAY FIELD TEST, unplanned and worth recording: THIS VERY ENTRY WAS REFUSED on its first attempt, because the Steward summary quoted shell syntax as prose while describing what the guard refuses. The guard fired correctly, named the override, and the override worked. A guard that refuses a description of itself and still leaves a sanctioned path is behaving exactly as designed.

VACUOUS-GREEN: dev/plans/runs/** is EXCLUDED from markdownlint (.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc, rationale "agent-emitted run logs, not maintained prose"), so scripts/agent-lint-md.sh exiting 0 says NOTHING about any file in that directory. The exclusion was written for machine-generated run logs, but the directory also holds MAINTAINED PROSE that the program depends on: STATUS-0.8.20.md (the board) and every STEWARD-SESSION-HANDOFF-*.md (the cold-start path). Discovered 2026-07-30 when a subagent correctly reported its own lint green as vacuous for a hand-off it had just written. Same class as the canary that hashed nothing on both sides and compared equal. Candidate fix: narrow the exclusion so it covers generated run logs only (output.json closure artifacts, codex transcripts) while linting the maintained prose - NOT a blanket un-exclude, which would light up a large backlog of genuinely-generated files. NOT blocking 0.8.20; do not attempt mid-release.

COMMISSION BRIEFS NEED A MECHANICAL FACT-CHECKER. Across three independent adversarial reviews of Steward-drafted briefs, every CRITICAL finding was the same defect class: a confidently-worded factual assertion the Steward did not measure. Instances: (a) Slice 40 v1 asserted release.yml fails to invoke cargo publish --dry-run - backwards, the TEST has swapped tier names, and the brief pre-authorised deleting an idempotency guard (seq-195); (b) Slice 40 v2 asserted a v* tag is the only irreversible publish path - false, workflow_dispatch with dry_run=false publishes for real and verify-release-gates only warns (seq-196); (c) Slice 39 asserted DenseReadiness is recorded signed in the allowlist - it appears ZERO times, and the instruction would have shipped a false sign-off onto docs.rs (seq-197); (d) both briefs asserted an AWAITING HITL SIGN-OFF string that was removed at seq-164 (seq-197). Plus ~17 off-by-N file:line cites across the same drafts. RESOLVE DOES NOT FIX THIS - tooling does, per the standing rule that a guardrail failure is fixed in the repo, not with a be-careful note. Proposal: a checker that parses a brief for (i) file:line citations, (ii) quoted source strings, (iii) claimed grep counts, and verifies each against HEAD, emitting a per-claim PASS/FAIL. Every one of the instances above is mechanically detectable. Natural home is scripts/, sibling to check-design-refs.sh. NOT blocking 0.8.20; the interim control is an adversarial review subagent per brief, which has caught 100 percent of these but costs a full review cycle each time.

PLACED AT 0.8.21 by HITL ruling (steward seq-198, 2026-07-30). TC-131, the commission-brief fact-checker first raised at seq-192, is BUILT AT 0.8.21 - not in 0.8.20. Rationale recorded with the ruling: only two commission briefs remain in 0.8.20, and the interim control (an adversarial review subagent per brief) has caught 100 percent of the defect class, so the tooling is not on the 0.8.20 critical path; and 0.8.21 can use the four recorded failure instances as TEST FIXTURES - seq-195 (Slice 40 v1: the cargo publish --dry-run assertion was backwards and the TEST had swapped tier names), seq-196 (Slice 40 v2: workflow_dispatch with dry_run=false publishes for real and verify-release-gates only warns), and seq-197 (Slice 39: DenseReadiness appears ZERO times in the allowlist, plus the AWAITING HITL SIGN-OFF string removed at seq-164). Scope is unchanged from seq-192: parse a brief for file:line citations, quoted source strings and claimed grep counts, and verify each against HEAD, emitting a per-claim PASS/FAIL. Natural home scripts/, sibling to check-design-refs.sh. NOTE 0.8.21 is an ODD micro, therefore OOB and label-only - building the checker there publishes nothing. Status stays open; this record places it, it does not close it.

TRANSCRIPT-HYGIENE GATE IS VACUOUS AT PRE-COMMIT - it did not fire on a real unredacted transcript I staged into a commit on 2026-07-30. Sequence: the Slice 39 orchestrator wrote codex transcripts into the PRIMARY checkout as well as its worktree; it redacted the branch copies (TC-86 predicate-2 hit, repaired with --redact) but the untracked primary copies stayed raw. My git add -A swept them in. The commit succeeded with only [pre-commit] md-safe-fix running - no hygiene arm fired at all. Measured afterwards on the swept blob: ZERO redaction markers, and scripts/check-transcript-hygiene.sh on that file exits 1 with "1 out-of-repo directory-inventory block, 36 lines of listing". The branch copy carries 1 REDACTED marker and is clean. So a file the gate DEMONSTRABLY rejects passed straight through commit into a PUBLIC repo. Recovery: the commit was never pushed (origin/main stayed at 3e9d6d12), main was reset, the tag holding the blob was deleted, the blob is unreachable and GC-eligible, and nothing left the machine. The Slice 39 orchestrator independently reported this same gap in its own closure - check-transcript-hygiene.sh returns 0 on an UNTRACKED transcript, so a pre-commit spot check is silently vacuous and only preflight --landing after committing is honest. This is the TC-86 mechanism recurring one layer up: the redaction step exists, but nothing between writing a transcript and committing it inspects the contents. Fix in the TOOLING, per the standing rule: the pre-commit hook must run the hygiene check over STAGED transcript paths, treating an untracked-but-staged file as in scope, and must fail closed rather than returning 0 when it finds nothing to check. A control proving it rejects a known-bad transcript is part of the fix - this gate has now been vacuous twice.
BOARD-CURRENCY BLIND SPOT: check-board-currency.sh certifies rc=0 on a board whose ladder row says a LANDED slice is NOT_STARTED. Distinct from the seq-204 fractional-id defect at :123.
body:
MEASURED at 46b9365e by the Steward, 2026-07-30. dev/plans/release-state-0.8.20.json records Slice 39 as LANDED at 91db34d8 with next_slice=40 and remaining_ladder=[40]. At the same commit, STATUS-0.8.20.md:76 (the Slice 39 ladder row) read "NOT_STARTED - the immediate next slice", :46 said "Next: Slice 39 (R-20-DOC), then Slice 40", :37 and :79 both said "Ladder remaining: 39 -> 40", and there was no Slice 39 close-record section. bash scripts/check-board-currency.sh exited 0 anyway, and so did the always-on CI board-currency job.

WHY IT PASSES: the check verifies that a landing merge subject of the form "merge(<version>): Slice[- ]<N>" has its short SHA cited LITERALLY SOMEWHERE in the board. 91db34d8 does appear on the board - but only inside the two GENERATED cells (the status-unblocks block and the immediate-next-action cell), which are rendered from the state file by check-release-state-views.sh. The generated half was therefore carrying the check while the entire hand-written half of the board contradicted it. Presence of a SHA is not currency of the row that SHA belongs to.

WHY IT MATTERS: the board is what a commissioning agent reads. A brief generated or hand-written against this board would have inherited "Slice 39 is the immediate next slice" - the TC-89 failure class, recurring one level up. It is also the same shape as the fractional-id class ruled at seq-204: a check that exits 0 while being silently wrong about which unit it is talking about.

DISTINCT FROM the SLICE-ID-HARDENING scope. That unit fixes check-board-currency.sh:123, where the slice-number capture takes "39" out of "Slice 39.5" and skips the real landing merge as superseded. This item is different: the capture is correct, the landing merge IS found, the SHA IS present, and the check still certifies a board that contradicts the state file on every hand-written row. Folding it into SLICE-ID-HARDENING would widen a ruled scope and is NOT done here.

CANDIDATE REMEDY (proposed, not ruled): have the check cross-read release-state-<version>.json and assert that for every id in "landed", the board does not describe it with a not-started/in-flight/next marker, and that remaining_ladder agrees with any "Ladder remaining:" prose. Any such arm must be proven non-vacuous with a control that makes it fail (trap 18) - a check added here that hashes nothing on both sides is the exact defect class this release has fought hardest.

PLACEMENT: unplaced. Natural home is 0.8.21 alongside TC-131 (the commission-brief fact-checker), which is the same "nothing mechanically catches a confidently-wrong assertion" family. HITL to rule.

summary: DO NOT BULK-REMOVE the "Requirement traceability" notes: there are TWELVE not eight, and several carry AUDIT FINDINGS that design_refs does not replace. Removal would destroy information.

CONTEXT. STEWARD-SESSION-HANDOFF-2026-07-30-A section 9 carries an owed item: "Eight Requirement traceability notes remain in dev/design/** from before the design_refs fix (d30ef52f). Removing them is owed. Do not write new ones."

MEASURED at 09d47443, and BOTH halves of that item need qualifying.

COUNT. grep -rn "Requirement traceability" dev/design/ returns TWELVE occurrences across TEN files, not eight: vector.md, embedder.md, errors.md (TWO), record-lifecycle-protocol/projection-registry-and-async-embed.md (TWO), 0.8.20-tc90-tc91-characterization.md, 0.8.20-tc57-write-race-characterization.md, 0.8.18-slice-0-vector-equivalence-publish-design.md, 0.8.18-slice-5-vector-equivalence-probe.md, 0.8.20-slice0-erasure-design.md, 0.7.0-vector-quant-pack1.md. Given that this session already produced one wrong "correction" of exactly that shape - seq-209, where 31 and 35 were both right under different conventions - the count discrepancy is recorded, NOT resolved by assertion.

THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT, which matters more than the count. These notes are NOT uniformly redundant linkage. The design_refs mechanism DOES supersede the linkage function - check-design-refs.sh reports 15 slices, 34 declared tokens, 2 exemptions, ZERO gaps - so "which requirement consults this doc" is now machine-checked and the prose restating it is genuinely redundant. CONSEQUENCE. A blanket removal keyed on the string "Requirement traceability" would delete real audit results along with the redundant linkage prose, and the audit results have no other home. The correct shape is a PER-NOTE triage: strip the linkage sentence, KEEP any audit finding, and give the kept material a heading that is not "Requirement traceability" so the ban on writing new ones still reads cleanly.

STATUS. NOT DONE, deliberately. Removing content from design docs is a record change and therefore an explicit HITL decision (steward hand-off section 5); it is not inside the reconcile mandate. The handoff item should be re-scoped from "removing them is owed" to "per-note triage is owed" before anyone acts on it. The ban on WRITING NEW ONES is unaffected and stands.

summary: TC-RUBRIC-7 COLLIDES WITH THE ORPHAN-MARKER SCAN: persisting a codex §9 transcript to its required TRACKED path reddens check-release-state-views.sh, because the scanner cannot tell a marker that DELIMITS a region from one merely QUOTED.
body:
MEASURED during SLICE-ID-HARDENING (landed 2008f529). codex quotes a literal generated-region BEGIN marker into its review transcript whenever it reads the board or the plan. check-release-state-views.sh enumerates candidate files with os.walk over the tree INCLUDING UNTRACKED FILES, so such a transcript is scanned and its quoted marker is reported as an ORPHAN generated-region marker. Measured rc=1 on 2 of the 3 transcripts that unit produced.

CONSEQUENCE: TC-RUBRIC-7 requires §9 transcripts to be persisted at a tracked path. Doing so would redden a governed gate on main PERMANENTLY. The two obligations are in direct conflict and one of them has to move. The unit correctly refused both bad options - it did not invent an ad-hoc redaction rule, and it did not weaken the scanner - and held the transcripts outside the tree instead, which means the release currently has §9 evidence that is NOT persisted where the rubric says it must be.

THE STEWARD REPRODUCED IT WITHIN MINUTES, which is the strongest evidence it needs a mechanical fix rather than a discipline note. Writing the Slice-ID-HARDENING close record into STATUS-0.8.20.md, I quoted the marker verbatim while DESCRIBING this very hazard; check-release-state-views.sh immediately returned rc=1 ORPHAN generated-region marker on the board itself. Any document that discusses the mechanism - a codex transcript, a close record, a design doc, a hand-off - is a landmine. "Just do not quote it" already failed on the person writing the warning.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES (proposed, none ruled): (a) exclude dev/plans/runs/codex/ from the orphan scan; (b) scan only TRACKED files, so untracked scratch cannot redden a gate - note this weakens the guard against a genuinely orphaned marker in a new file; (c) require the marker to be at line-start in a markdown comment context rather than anywhere in the line; (d) an explicit escape convention for quoting markers in prose. Any fix MUST be proven non-vacuous with a control that makes it fail, and must not stop detecting a REAL orphan - that is the whole purpose of the check.

HITL RULING OWED. Until then, §9 transcripts stay out of the tree and TC-RUBRIC-7 is knowingly unmet for this release.

summary: TC-121 THIRD INSTANCE: seat-path-guard.sh matched a path string appearing as a JSON VALUE inside a closure payload and blocked the write. Prose is not a write target; the guard should match the resolved path, not payload contents.
body:
THIRD recorded instance (the first two were during Slice 33). At the very end of SLICE-ID-HARDENING the orchestrator could not write its closure output.json: the guard denied with "the orchestrator seat may not write ... it is under a tests/ path segment", because the closure JSON quoted the path scripts/tests/test_sealed_worktree_guard.sh AS A STRING VALUE in its payload. Nothing was being written to that path.

The orchestrator diagnosed it correctly and worked around it by writing to scratch rather than softening the guard - the right call, and exactly what brief §5 required. But it cost real time at the end of an already long unit, and it will recur: EVERY closure record names the test files the unit touched, so a closure that mentions a test path is structurally at risk.

COMPOUNDING FACT WORTH RECORDING: the specific path that triggered it, scripts/tests/test_sealed_worktree_guard.sh, existed only because the STEWARD wrote a test source it should have commissioned (seq-213, the boundary breach the HITL flagged). The breach and this block are the same event seen twice.

REMEDY DIRECTION (proposed, not ruled): the guard should decide on the RESOLVED WRITE TARGET - Edit/Write file_path, and for Bash the actual redirection/target of the command - not on any occurrence of a protected path substring anywhere in the payload. A guard that reads its own subject matter as a violation will keep firing on the documents that describe it, which is the same shape as TC-135 recorded this same day. Fix the tooling, do not add a note telling people to avoid mentioning paths.

summary: A STALE NATIVE MODULE MAKES test-python LOOK CATASTROPHICALLY RED (40 collection errors) WHEN IT IS SIMPLY UNRUNNABLE. It needs a FOURTH report state: UNKNOWN-requires-rebuild. Not TC-97.
body:
MEASURED 2026-07-30 at fcae308e, from the primary checkout, read-only, with FATHOMDB_TESTS_ALLOW_REBUILD deliberately unset.

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q src/python/tests gives "Interrupted: 40 errors during collection". Every one is the same ImportError: cannot import name IllegalTransitionError from fathomdb._fathomdb (src/python/fathomdb/_fathomdb.abi3.so). The compiled native module is STALE - it predates the 0.8.19 Phase-1 lifecycle symbols. NOT ONE of the 40 is a test failure.

RULED OUT: this is NOT TC-97s pythonpath shadowing. Re-running with -o pythonpath= from a neutral cwd (/tmp) produces the IDENTICAL 40 errors.

WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW. Slice 39.5s whole deliverable is the TRUE red list, local and CI, and that list is the input to a single HITL disposition decision. An agent that runs test-python read-only and records "40 errors" publishes a FALSE RED into the exact document the decision will be made from - the failure class this release has fought hardest. The suites real state is UNKNOWN, not red.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT. agent-test.sh:231-236 authorises FATHOMDB_TESTS_ALLOW_REBUILD=1 and a conftest maturin develop when the interpreter is the checkouts own .venv. For the PYTHON suite that rebuild is a PREREQUISITE, not a convenience: without it the suite cannot even collect. So a red list needs FOUR states, not three - PASSED, FAILED, SKIPPED-prerequisite-absent, and UNKNOWN-requires-the-sanctioned-rebuild.

COMPOUNDING CONSTRAINT: the rebuild cannot simply be run to resolve it. In a WORKTREE it rebinds the shared virtualenv to the worktree source tree - the named agent-worktree-stale-base-trap, which has already cost two slices - so a worktree baseline can NEVER cover this suite honestly. In the PRIMARY it is sanctioned but is a build, which is neither the Stewards work nor a reporting units.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BASELINE: the true local red list has TWO principled, nameable holes - the venv-gated suites a worktree cannot reach without the forbidden rebind, and test-python whose result is meaningless without a rebuild nobody is authorised to perform mid-unit. A list that names what it could not reach, and why, is worth more than one that looks complete. Recorded so a later session does not "fix" this by rebuilding blind or by filing 40 phantom failures.

summary: LEAD ON PUBLISH GATE (i): 5 of the 7 pyright errors that kill CI verify+security are STUB-vs-SOURCE DRIFT in a TRACKED file - symbols present in the Rust binding source and ABSENT from the committed _fathomdb.pyi.
body:
MEASURED 2026-07-30 at 59ec30c7, from the primary checkout.

bash scripts/agent-typecheck.sh on UNMODIFIED main is rc=1 with exactly SEVEN errors - the same seven the record says kill the ci.yml verify and security jobs in BOOTSTRAP, before their real work runs. They reproduce LOCALLY, which is the first useful thing to know: this is not a CI-environment problem.

THE DRIFT, measured. The three symbols named in five of the seven errors exist in the Rust binding source - dense_disabled 11 occurrences, dense_disabled_reason 4, vector_equivalence_refusal_count 2, under src/rust/crates/fathomdb-py/src/. In the TYPE STUB the checker actually reads, src/python/fathomdb/_fathomdb.pyi, dense_disabled appears ZERO times. The five errors are all of the form "Cannot access attribute X for class Engine" / "for class OpenReport".

WHY THIS EXPLAINS CI EXACTLY. _fathomdb.pyi is TRACKED - I verified with git ls-files --error-unmatch - so CI reads the identical stale file and fails identically. By contrast _fathomdb.abi3.so is NOT tracked, so the separate local staleness recorded at TC-136 (the .so built 2026-07-09 against binding source last touched 2026-07-28, 19 days apart, missing IllegalTransitionError) is a LOCAL-ENVIRONMENT artifact and a DIFFERENT problem. Do not conflate them: TC-136 is an untracked build artifact, TC-137 is a committed file that is wrong in the repository.

SCOPE, stated honestly. FIVE of seven are this shape. The other two are NOT and must not be assumed to share the cause: graph.py:153 is an assignability error between fathomdb._fathomdb.IdSpace and fathomdb.types.IdSpace - a duplicate-type problem, not a missing attribute - and the seventh is an unexpected `reason` parameter in test_vector_equivalence_probe.py.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN. I have NOT regenerated the stub and re-run pyright, so "regenerating the stub clears five of seven" is a well-evidenced HYPOTHESIS, not a measured fact. State it that way. The determination - and the fix - belong to whoever owns the disposition of the CI baseline, not to Slice 39.5, which reports and does not fix.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. Publish gate (i) (seq-202 as amended by seq-211) requires every ci.yml job THAT EXECUTED to conclude success. Four jobs fail; verify and security are two of them and both die in bootstrap on precisely these seven errors. If the stub-drift hypothesis holds, a stub regeneration would clear two of the four reds and materially advance a gate that currently blocks the first real publish since v0.8.9. That makes this the highest-value lead currently open on the release.

summary: graph.search_expand has TWO mapper defects: it passes the NATIVE PyO3 IdSpace into a dataclass field typed as the SDK IdSpace, and it silently DROPS source_id and ce_score. The second is invisible to pyright and contradicts the SearchHit docstring.
body:
MEASURED by a commissioned read-only probe and re-verified by the Steward directly from source.

DEFECT 1 - TYPE. graph.py builds SearchHit(id=h.id, ...) passing the native fathomdb._fathomdb.IdSpace straight through, while types.SearchHit.id is annotated as the fathomdb.types.IdSpace frozen dataclass. engine.py:488 does it correctly (id=IdSpace(space=hit.id.space, value=hit.id.value)). Measured at runtime: engine.search hits give isinstance(sdk IdSpace)=True, graph.search_expand hits give False. Consequences: equality between hits from the two read paths fails, and dataclasses.asdict/astuple/replace break on graph hits. This is the SEVENTH pyright error and the ONE a stub edit cannot clear - pyright is nominal for dataclasses. A stub-level workaround exists (declare the native class a subclass of the SDK dataclass) and was MEASURED to silence it; it is REJECTED because issubclass is False at runtime, so it would encode a lie to hide a live defect.

DEFECT 2 - PROVENANCE, and invisible to pyright. The same mapper omits source_id and ce_score entirely. Both fields have None defaults, so nothing type-checks as wrong. Measured on a real DB: native search_expand hit source_id=probe:1, SDK-returned hit source_id=None. The SearchHit docstring explicitly documents that source_id is None ONLY when the stored row really has NULL provenance - written before 0.8.20, or a governed row spared by the step-21 backfill under the TC-11 pin. So the SDK returns an answer that is not merely absent but MISLEADING per its own contract, on the field the erasure axis runs through.

PLACEMENT. Defect 1 is unavoidably in Slice 40 - it is the last pyright error and publish gate (i) cannot pass without it. Defect 2 is NOT on Slice 39.5s baseline list and its placement is UNPLACED and owed to the HITL. Steward recommendation on record: fix both, since they are the same two lines of the same mapper. NOT placed by the Steward - the seq-220 lesson.

Origin: defect 1 dates to 6616db93 (0.8.19 Slice 15, C-2 typed SearchHit.id). Defect 2 predates it (ccfb2191, 2026-06-13).

summary: test-md-generators is RED in the primary checkout: context-clarity.sh uses $PRUNE_EXPR UNQUOTED in find, so its glob patterns expand against the repo root whenever matching local dirs exist. NOT on Slice 39.5s baseline list.
body:
A REAL bug that is ENVIRONMENT-TRIGGERED, found by a commissioned probe and proven decisively by it.

MECHANISM. PRUNE_EXPR holds find predicates containing literal glob patterns (-path */node_modules -o -path */__pycache__ and six more). It is then interpolated into find UNQUOTED, so the shell word-splits AND glob-expands it against the repo root before find ever sees it. Traced with bash -x: -path */node_modules became -path node_modules/node_modules typescript/node_modules; */__pycache__ became scripts/__pycache__; */.pytest_cache and */.ruff_cache likewise. find then errors on the stray bare argument, returns an empty list with nonzero status, set -e kills the script, and no .md is produced. The generator failure is SWALLOWED by a || true at test_md_generators.sh:76, so only the missing output file surfaces - the real error never reaches the report.

PROOF. bash -f context-clarity.sh __probe_noglob (globbing disabled, nothing else changed) returns rc=0 and produces both outputs.

WHY IT WAS NOT ON THE 39.5 BASELINE. It fires only when the repo root contains a directory matching one of the eight patterns. Those are untracked local artifacts, so the red is present in the primary checkout and absent where they are not - which is why the 39.5 run, and the CI reachability, differ. Whether a pristine ubuntu-latest checkout produces a matching path is UNDETERMINED; bootstrap.sh npm-installs a root node_modules but not a nested node_modules/node_modules.

PLACEMENT UNPLACED and owed to the HITL. The fix is a one-line quoting correction. NOTE it also means the local red list and the CI red list are NOT the same list, which is itself worth carrying.

summary: FOUR typed-error classes are missing their __init__ in the stub - the identical gap to the seventh pyright error, merely not yet exercised. MEASURED: 8 new pyright errors the moment any code constructs them with their documented kwargs.
body:
errors.py installs typed inits at import time via _install_typed_init on IllegalTransitionError (from_state, to_state, legal), NotLifecycleAddressableError (id_space), ErasureIncompleteError (stage, detail) and ProjectionDestructiveError (name, delta). The stub declares only the ATTRIBUTES, not the __init__ signatures. Measured with a throwaway probe file: constructing them with those kwargs yields 8 new reportCallIssue errors.

This is exactly the shape of the existing seventh error (VectorEquivalenceMismatchError with reason=), which is red today only because one test happens to construct it. The other four are latent landmines that will redden CI for the next person who uses the documented API.

Zero marginal cost to close: same file, same edit as the TC-137 stub sync. Steward recommendation on record is to close it in that edit. PLACEMENT UNPLACED - owed to the HITL.

SEPARATE FIDELITY NOTE, not fixed and not proposed here: _install_typed_init defaults every unpassed payload field to None, so at runtime these payload attributes can be None although the stub types several of them as non-optional str. That is a wider surface decision, pre-existing across all typed error leaves, and is NOT part of unbreaking CI.

summary: CI TEST-COVERAGE BLIND SPOT: there is NO full-workspace cargo test on Linux anywhere in ci.yml, and rust-macos runs WITHOUT --no-fail-fast so it aborts early. rust-windows is the only job that reliably surfaces the full Rust set - and it has been ~90 percent red since it first ran.
body:
VERIFIED BY THE STEWARD from ci.yml directly, not taken from the probe report.

THE GAP. cargo test appears four times in ci.yml. Two are default-embedder-tests running NAMED TARGETS ONLY (-p fathomdb-engine --test eu5b_lockflip and -p fathomdb-cli --test cli_warm_cache). The other two are rust-windows (cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast) and rust-macos (cargo test --workspace, NO --no-fail-fast). So the full Rust workspace suite runs on Linux ONLY inside the verify job, via agent-verify.sh then agent-test.sh then test-rust.

WHY THAT MATTERS RIGHT NOW. verify has been dying in Bootstrap dev tooling since roughly 2026-07-09 on the seven pyright errors, so the Linux Rust workspace suite has NOT EXECUTED IN CI for about three weeks. Meanwhile rust-macos aborts at the first failure (usually the TC-72 lock-holder flake) before reaching later tests, and rust-windows - the one job with --no-fail-fast, which is the sole reason the tc57 red was ever visible - has been failing ~90 percent of runs.

CONSEQUENCE: the engine test signal in CI has been substantially degraded for three weeks, entering the first publish since v0.8.9.

STEWARD RECOMMENDATION ON RECORD: 0.8.21, not Slice 40. Both fixes WIDEN VISIBILITY, which under the ruled fix-everything gate means importing an unknown quantity of new red into a unit that has already grown twice and may not be split. Neither affects what 0.8.20 actually publishes (x86_64-linux only, dist-tag next). PLACEMENT UNPLACED - owed to the HITL.

Observed while dating the verify red. CI run 30566757420 installed pyright 1.1.411; the local .venv holds 1.1.409. Nothing pins the floor tighter than 1.1.380.

Always the identical site: _vector_kind_registered in test_slice20c_flush_barrier.py reached from test_late_enrolment_backfills_rows_a_no_embedder_session_stranded.

summary: PLACED IN SLICE 40 by HITL 2026-07-30. TC-91 is the cause of the rust-windows red: commit_projection_outcomes opens DEFERRED while commit_batch opens IMMEDIATE. MEASURED 83 failures / 92 executed Windows runs = 90.2 percent - NOT a flake.
body:
The rust-windows red was reported-only for several sessions and never diagnosed. A commissioned probe bucketed it and the Steward verified every load-bearing claim from source.

BUCKET (c): a platform-neutral defect that Windows timing exposes past a Linux-calibrated bound. Definitively NOT the lock-holder flake class - no DatabaseLocked panic, and macOS is 21/21 green on identical source. NOT a timing artifact: constraining cores locally with taskset moved the number 12 percent, not 250.

MECHANISM, STEWARD-VERIFIED. TransactionBehavior::Immediate appears EXACTLY ONCE in the whole engine - commit_batch at lib.rs:18706, TC-57s fix. commit_projection_outcomes at lib.rs:13878 opens a plain connection.transaction(), i.e. DEFERRED, and has the same read-then-upgrade shape - the residual risk TC-57s own design doc named and deliberately left. Its error is DISCARDED at lib.rs:12780 and lib.rs:12893 via let _ = , so a failed commit leaves terminal IS NULL, the row is re-dispatched, and it re-embeds. Re-embeds are therefore the only observable.

THE DEFECT SHIPS ON LINUX. Windows repeat_embeds median 370 over 200 rows; LINUX measures 105 to 119 - roughly every other row embedded twice, on the platform 0.8.20 actually publishes. That is TC-91(a), the ~50 percent baseline duplicate rate, open and unowned since Slice 21. Windows is the same defect at 3-5x because lock occupancy is 81 percent there versus 60 percent on Linux.

FIX SHAPE: (1) stop discarding the error at 12780/12893 so the cause is MEASURED rather than inferred - the one inference in the chain; (2) open commit_projection_outcomes IMMEDIATE, the same one-line change TC-57 applied to the sibling. With BEGIN IMMEDIATE the busy handler is consulted, so the existing 5s timeout absorbs contention.

ACCEPTANCE BAR: N=5 consecutive green rust-windows runs. At 90.2 percent failure a single green happens by luck about 10 percent of the time. No local Windows box exists; CI is the only sufficient check, at 10-15 minutes per run, non-parallelisable, unverifiable before pushing. THIS IS SLICE 40s LONG POLE.

HONEST LIMIT: nobody can say whether TC-57s fix CAUSED the Windows excursion. The instrument landed in the same commit series, so there is no Windows before. The mechanism predicts it worsened it; that is a prediction, not a measurement.

TEST HYGIENE FOUND: the assertion doc comment claims a 10 percent bound while the code asserts 100 percent (stale), and the ANONYMOUS arm carries no repeat_embeds assertion at all - which is why only half the red was ever visible.

summary: QUANTIFIED: a stub-only edit clears SIX of the seven pyright errors, MEASURED. The seventh is not a stub defect at all - it is the graph.py mapper bug now tracked as TC-138. Also: the stub CANNOT be regenerated; it is hand-maintained.
body:
Measured by a commissioned probe against a scratch copy of src/python, using the exact pyright invocation agent-typecheck.sh uses, after first reproducing the 7-error baseline in the copy. Stub-only edit gives rc=1 with exactly one error remaining; stub plus the graph.py fix gives rc=0.

THE SIX. Engine.dense_disabled, .dense_disabled_reason and .vector_equivalence_refusal_count are #[pymethods] on PyEngine and simply absent from the stub. OpenReport.dense_disabled and .dense_disabled_reason are get_all fields on PyOpenReport, absent from the stub. VectorEquivalenceMismatchError needs an __init__ with reason= - note this is a PYTHON-side construct installed by errors.py _install_typed_init, NOT a Rust export, so an implementer reading only lib.rs would wrongly conclude the test is at fault and delete the kwarg.

THE SEVENTH is graph.py:153 - see TC-138. Pyright is nominal for dataclasses so no stub relaxation makes the native and SDK IdSpace assignable; the only stub-level silencer would assert a subclass relationship that is FALSE at runtime.

ORIGIN, Steward-verified: errors 1-5 and 7 all trace to ONE commit, f2f843ed (2026-07-09, 0.8.18 Slice 5) - engine.py, the test and the Rust binding landed together and the stub alone was not updated.

SURFACE AUDIT, otherwise clean: 24/24 classes, 18/18 functions with matching signatures and defaults, 28/28 exception leaves with correct bases, and field-level agreement on 22 structs. OpenReport was the only field-level gap.

summary: PLACED IN SLICE 40 by HITL 2026-07-30, BOTH HALVES: the IdSpace conversion AND the source_id/ce_score restore. The Steward recommended fixing both and did not place either.
body:
The IdSpace half was unavoidable regardless - it is the seventh pyright error and publish gate (i) cannot pass without it. The provenance half was a genuine scope decision: it is NOT on Slice 39.5s baseline list, pyright cannot see it, and it could have been deferred.

HITL ruled BOTH into Slice 40. Steward reasoning offered and accepted: they are the same two lines of the same mapper, and shipping a known provenance-dropping defect in a function just edited - on the release whose erasure axis IS provenance - is the worse outcome.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE for the brief: the fix is to add IdSpace to the fathomdb.types import block in graph.py and build id=IdSpace(space=h.id.space, value=h.id.value), plus pass source_id=h.source_id and ce_score=h.ce_score - matching what engine.py already does at its own SearchHit construction. RED-first: a test asserting isinstance(hit.id, types.IdSpace) and a populated source_id from search_expand.

RISK carried into the brief: this may flip a currently-PASSING test that asserts todays wrong behaviour. Run the full Python suite after, not just the new test.

summary: PRODUCT-FACING: opening a stdlib sqlite3 connection to the DB file while a FathomDB Engine is open IN THE SAME PROCESS is unsafe - the engine bundles its own SQLite and Pythons links the system one, and two copies in one process steal each others POSIX locks. Consumer-facing docs gap.
body:
Surfaced by the OOS-18 fix-shape probe and Steward-verified from source.

MECHANISM. src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/Cargo.toml declares rusqlite with features = ["bundled"], so the engine links its OWN statically-bundled SQLite; Pythons sqlite3 links the system libsqlite3 (3.45.1 on this box). SQLites WAL concurrency contract is defined over PROCESSES, and its workaround for POSIX advisory-lock semantics - where close() of ANY fd on an inode drops that processs locks on it - lives in a per-library-copy inode cache the two copies do not share. Two copies in one process therefore steal each others locks and invalidate each others -shm mappings.

MEASURED: an in-process stdlib probe against a live-WAL DB while the engine is open SIGBUSes 25 times in 60; the identical probe in a CHILD process, 0 in 60.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY A TEST ISSUE. OOS-18 is classified in-repo as a HARNESS hazard, not an engine defect. That is correct ABOUT THE TEST. But the same configuration is reachable by any consumer of the Python binding who opens a stdlib sqlite3 connection - for inspection, migration, a dashboard - while holding an open Engine in the same process. Reading from a SEPARATE process (the sqlite3 CLI, a DB browser, eval/verify_embed_db.py) is safe.

WHAT IS OWED: a consumer-facing note on the Python surface stating the constraint. NOT Slice 40s - the slice fixes the test, and the Steward is not placing this. NOTE the TS side already states the discipline explicitly: the slice20c mirror in src/ts/tests declares node:sqlite is used only as a READ oracle on a CLOSED database. The Python test had no equivalent rule and drifted.

PLACEMENT UNPLACED - owed to the HITL.
